bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 【後周紀五】起著雍敦牂，盡屠維協洽，凡二年。

translations.literal: [Later Zhou Records 5] Beginning at Zhuanyong Dunzhang, through Tuwei Xieqia; two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Later Zhou Records 5] From Zhuanyong Dunzhang through Tuwei Xieqia—two years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙酉，廢匡國軍。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on yiyou, the Kuangguo Army was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on yiyou, Emperor Shizong abolished the Kuangguo Army.

sentences.zh: 唐改元中興。

translations.literal: Tang changed the era name to Zhongxing.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Tang changed the era name to Zhongxing.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，右龍武將軍王漢璋奏克海州。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Right Dragon Martial General Wang Hanzhang reported the capture of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Right Dragon Martial General Wang Hanzhang reported that Haizhou had been captured.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以侍衛馬軍都指揮使韓令坤權揚州軍府事。

translations.literal: On jichou, the Palace Cavalry Commander-in-Chief Han Lingkun was appointed acting military administrator of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Emperor Shizong appointed Palace Cavalry Commander-in-Chief Han Lingkun acting military administrator of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 上欲引戰艦自淮入江，阻北神堰，不得渡；

translations.literal: The emperor wished to lead warships from the Huai into the Yangtze, but was blocked by the Beishen weir and could not pass through;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to lead warships from the Huai into the Yangtze, but the Beishen weir blocked the way and they could not pass through;

sentences.zh: 欲鑿楚州西北鸛水以通其道，遣使行視，還言地形不便，計功甚多。

translations.literal: He wished to cut through the Guan River northwest of Chuzhou to open a passage, and sent envoys to survey the route; they returned saying the terrain was unsuitable and the labor required would be very great.
translations.idiomatic: He planned to cut a channel through the Guan River northwest of Chuzhou to open a passage and sent envoys to survey the route; they returned reporting that the terrain was unsuitable and the project would require enormous labor.

sentences.zh: 上自往視之，授以規畫，發楚州民夫浚之，旬日而成，用功甚省。

translations.literal: The emperor went in person to inspect it, gave directions for the plan, mobilized corvée labor from Chuzhou to dredge it, and in ten days it was completed, with labor very sparingly used.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went in person to inspect the site, laid out the plan himself, mobilized corvée labor from Chuzhou to dredge the channel, and completed it in ten days at remarkably little cost in labor.

sentences.zh: 巨艦百艘皆達於江，唐人大驚，以為神。

translations.literal: A hundred great ships all reached the Yangtze; the people of Tang were greatly alarmed and regarded it as divine.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred great warships all reached the Yangtze; the Southern Tang were astonished and took it for a miracle.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，拔靜海軍，始通吳越之路。

translations.literal: On renchen, the Jinghai Army was taken, and the route to Wu and Yue was opened for the first time.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Zhou forces captured the Jinghai Army post, opening the land route to Wu-Yue for the first time.

sentences.zh: 先是帝遣左諫議大夫長安尹日就等使吳越，語之曰：「卿今去雖泛海，比還，淮南已平，當陸歸耳。」

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor had sent Left Remonstrance Counselor Yin Riujiu of Chang'an and others as envoys to Wu-Yue, telling them, "Though you go now by sea, by the time you return Huainan will already be pacified and you will come back by land."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had sent Left Remonstrance Counselor Yin Riujiu of Chang'an and others as envoys to Wu-Yue, telling them, "Though you sail there by sea, by the time you return Huainan will already be pacified and you will travel home overland."

sentences.zh: 已而果然。

translations.literal: And so it indeed came to pass.
translations.idiomatic: And so it indeed came to pass.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，蜀右補闕章九齡見蜀主，言政事不治，由奸佞在朝。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Shu Right Supplementation Censor Zhang Jiuling saw the Shu ruler and said that government was not well ordered because treacherous flatterers were at court.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Shu Right Supplementation Censor Zhang Jiuling had an audience with the Shu ruler and charged that government was in disorder because treacherous flatterers held sway at court.

sentences.zh: 蜀主問奸佞為誰，指李昊、王昭遠以對。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler asked who the treacherous flatterers were; he pointed to Li Hao and Wang Zhaoyuan in reply.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shu ruler asked who the flatterers were, Jiuling named Li Hao and Wang Zhaoyuan.

sentences.zh: 蜀主怒，以九齡為毀斥大臣，貶維州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: The Shu ruler was angry, took Jiuling to be slandering high ministers, and demoted him to Recorder of Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler was enraged, judged Jiuling to be slandering senior ministers, and demoted him to Recorder of Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 周兵攻楚州，逾四旬，唐楚州防禦使張彥卿固守不下。

translations.literal: Zhou troops attacked Chuzhou; after more than forty days, Tang Chuzhou defense commissioner Zhang Yanqing held firm and the city was not taken.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou troops besieged Chuzhou; for more than forty days Southern Tang defense commissioner Zhang Yanqing held the city and it did not fall.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，帝自督諸將攻之，宿於城下。

translations.literal: On yisi, the emperor personally directed the generals in the assault and lodged beneath the walls.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Emperor Shizong personally directed the generals in the assault and camped beneath the city walls.

sentences.zh: 丁未，克之。

translations.literal: On dingwei, it was captured.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, the city fell.

sentences.zh: 彥卿與都監鄭昭業猶帥眾拒戰，矢刃皆盡，彥卿舉繩床以斗而死，所部千餘人，至死無一人降者。

translations.literal: Yanqing and superintendent Zheng Zhaoye still led the troops in resisting; arrows and blades were all exhausted; Yanqing lifted a rope bed to fight and died; of his command of more than a thousand men, to the end not one surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing and superintendent Zheng Zhaoye still led their men in resistance until arrows and blades were spent; Yanqing seized a rope bed and fought on until he was killed; of his command of more than a thousand, not one surrendered even at death.

sentences.zh: 高保融遣指揮使魏璘將戰船百艘東下會伐唐，至於鄂州。

translations.literal: Gao Baorong sent commander Wei Lin with a hundred warships eastward to join the campaign against Tang, reaching Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Baorong sent commander Wei Lin east with a hundred warships to join the campaign against Southern Tang, reaching Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，蜀置永寧軍於果州，以通州隸之。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Shu established the Yongning Army at Guozhou and placed Tongzhou under it.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Later Shu established the Yongning Army at Guozhou and placed Tongzhou under its jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 唐以天長為雄州，以建武軍使易文贇為刺史。

translations.literal: Tang made Tianchang into Xiong Prefecture and appointed Jianwu Army commissioner Yi Wenyun as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Tang redesignated Tianchang as Xiong Prefecture and appointed Jianwu Army commissioner Yi Wenyun prefect.

sentences.zh: 二月，甲寅，文贇舉城降。

translations.literal: In the second month, on jiayin, Wenyun surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jiayin, Yi Wenyun surrendered the city with all its defenders.

sentences.zh: 戊午，帝發楚州。

translations.literal: On wuwu, the emperor departed from Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Emperor Shizong marched out from Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，至揚州，命韓令坤發丁夫萬餘，築故城之東南隅為小城以治之。

translations.literal: On dingmao, he reached Yangzhou and ordered Han Lingkun to mobilize more than ten thousand corvée laborers to build a small city in the southeast corner of the old walls for administration.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, he reached Yangzhou and ordered Han Lingkun to mobilize more than ten thousand laborers to build a small administrative city in the southeast corner of the old walls.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，黃州刺史司超奏與控鶴右廂都指揮使王審琦攻唐舒州，擒其刺史施仁望。

translations.literal: On yihai, Huangzhou prefect Si Chao reported that with Right Column Crane-Control Commander Wang Shenqi he had attacked Tang Shuzhou and captured its prefect Shi Renwang.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Huangzhou prefect Si Chao reported that he and Right Column Crane-Control Commander Wang Shenqi had attacked Southern Tang Shuzhou and captured prefect Shi Renwang.

sentences.zh: 丙子，建雄節度使真定楊廷璋奏敗北漢兵於隰州城下。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Jianxiong military governor Yang Tingzhang of Zhending reported defeating Northern Han troops below the walls of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Jianxiong military governor Yang Tingzhang of Zhending reported defeating Northern Han troops below the walls of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 時隰州刺史孫議暴卒，廷璋謂都監、閒廄使李謙溥曰：「今大駕南征，澤州無守將，河東必生心。

translations.literal: At the time Xizhou prefect Sun Yi died suddenly; Tingzhang said to superintendent and Inner Stables commissioner Li Qianbo, "Now that the great army is campaigning south, Ze Prefecture has no defending commander; Hedong is sure to harbor designs.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xizhou prefect Sun Yi died suddenly; Tingzhang told superintendent and Inner Stables commissioner Li Qianbo, "With the emperor campaigning south, Ze Prefecture has no defending commander; Hedong is sure to take advantage.

sentences.zh: 若奏請待報，則孤城危矣！」

translations.literal: If we memorialize and wait for a reply, the isolated city will be in peril!"
translations.idiomatic: If we wait on memorial and reply, this isolated city will be lost!"

sentences.zh: 即牒謙溥權隰州事，謙溥至則修守備。

translations.literal: He at once issued a dispatch appointing Qianbo acting administrator of Xizhou; when Qianbo arrived he repaired the defenses.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately issued a dispatch appointing Qianbo acting administrator of Xizhou; on arrival Qianbo set about repairing the defenses.

sentences.zh: 未幾，北漢兵果至，諸將請速救之。

translations.literal: Before long Northern Han troops indeed arrived, and the generals asked to go quickly to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Northern Han troops did arrive, and the generals urged an immediate rescue.

sentences.zh: 廷璋曰：「隰州城堅將良，未易克也。」

translations.literal: Tingzhang said, "Xizhou's walls are strong and its commander capable; it will not be easy to take."
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhang said, "Xizhou's walls are strong and its commander capable; they will not take it easily."

sentences.zh: 北漢攻城久不下，廷璋度其疲睏無備，潛與謙溥約，各募死士百餘夜襲其營，北漢兵驚潰，斬首千餘級，北漢兵遂解去。

translations.literal: The Northern Han siege dragged on without success; Tingzhang judged them weary and off guard, secretly agreed with Qianbo, each recruited more than a hundred dare-to-die men for a night raid on their camp; Northern Han troops were startled and routed, more than a thousand heads were taken, and the Northern Han army then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Han siege wore on without success; Tingzhang judged them exhausted and unprepared, secretly coordinated with Qianbo, and each side recruited more than a hundred dare-to-die men for a night raid on the enemy camp; the Northern Han were routed in panic, more than a thousand heads were taken, and the besieging army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬午朔，帝如泰州。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the renwu new moon, the emperor went to Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the renwu new moon, Emperor Shizong went to Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，唐大赦，改元交泰。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Tang proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Jiaotai.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Southern Tang proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Jiaotai.

sentences.zh: 唐太弟景遂前後凡十表辭位，且言：「今國危不能扶，請出就籓鎮。

translations.literal: Tang's Grand Younger Brother Jing Sui in all submitted ten memorials declining his position, saying moreover, "The state is now in peril and I cannot support it; I ask to go out to a frontier fief.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Tang Grand Younger Brother Li Jing Sui had submitted ten memorials declining his position, saying, "The state is in peril and I cannot save it; let me withdraw to a frontier fief.

sentences.zh: 燕王弘冀嫡長有軍功，宜為嗣，謹奉上太弟寶冊。」

translations.literal: Prince of Yan Hongji is the eldest legitimate son and has military merit; he should be heir; I respectfully offer up the Grand Younger Brother's seals of office."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yan Li Hongji is the eldest legitimate son and has military merit; he should be heir; I respectfully surrender the Grand Younger Brother's seals of office."

sentences.zh: 齊王景達亦以敗軍辭元帥。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Jing Da also resigned the post of commander-in-chief on account of defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Li Jing Da also resigned the post of commander-in-chief, citing his defeat.

sentences.zh: 唐主乃立景遂為晉王，加天策上將軍、江南西道兵馬元帥、洪州大督都、太尉、尚書令，以景達為浙西道元帥、潤州大都督。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler then installed Jing Sui as Prince of Jin, adding Celestial Stratagem Grand General, Jiangnan West Circuit military commander-in-chief, Hongzhou supreme commander, Grand Commandant, and Director of the Imperial Secretariat; he made Jing Da Zhexi Circuit commander-in-chief and great governor of Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler then created Jing Sui Prince of Jin with the titles Celestial Stratagem Grand General, Jiangnan West Circuit military commander-in-chief, Hongzhou supreme commander, Grand Commandant, and Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and appointed Jing Da Zhexi Circuit commander-in-chief and great governor of Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 景達以浙西方用兵，固辭，改撫州大都督。

translations.literal: Jing Da, on the ground that Zhexi was at war, firmly declined and was changed to great governor of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Da firmly declined on the ground that Zhexi was still at war and was reassigned as great governor of Fuzhou instead.

sentences.zh: 立弘冀為皇太子，參決庶政。

translations.literal: Hongji was installed as crown prince to participate in deciding routine government.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongji was installed as crown prince with authority to participate in routine government.

sentences.zh: 弘冀為人猜忌嚴刻，景遂左右有未出東宮者，立斥逐之。

translations.literal: Hongji was by nature suspicious and harsh; any of Jing Sui's attendants who had not yet left the Eastern Palace were at once driven out.
translations.idiomatic: Hongji was suspicious and harsh by nature; any of Jing Sui's attendants who had not yet left the Eastern Palace were immediately expelled.

sentences.zh: 其弟安定公從嘉畏之，不敢預事，專以經籍自娛。

translations.literal: His younger brother Duke of Anding Congjia feared him, dared not take part in affairs, and devoted himself solely to the classics for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Duke of Anding Li Congjia feared him, dared not involve himself in politics, and devoted himself to the classics for solace.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，上如迎鑾鎮，屢至江口，遣水軍擊唐兵，破之。

translations.literal: On xinmao, the emperor went to Yingluan post, repeatedly came to the river mouth, sent the navy to strike Tang troops, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, the emperor went to Yingluan post, repeatedly visited the river mouth, sent the navy against Southern Tang forces, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 上聞唐戰艦數百艘泊東水布州，將趣海口扼蘇、杭路，遣殿前都虞候慕容延釗將步騎，右神武統軍宋延渥將水軍，循江而下。

translations.literal: The emperor heard that several hundred Tang warships were moored at Dongshuibuzhou and would make for the estuary to choke the Suzhou and Hangzhou route; he sent Palace Front military inspector Murong Yanzhao with infantry and cavalry, and Right Divine Martial army commander Song Yanwo with the navy, down the river.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that several hundred Southern Tang warships lay at Dongshuibuzhou and intended to seize the estuary and block the route to Suzhou and Hangzhou, he sent Palace Front military inspector Murong Yanzhao with infantry and cavalry and Right Divine Martial army commander Song Yanwo with the navy downriver against them.

sentences.zh: 甲午，延釗奏大破唐兵於東水布州。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Yanzhao reported a great defeat of Tang troops at Dongshuibuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Yanzhao reported a great victory over Southern Tang forces at Dongshuibuzhou.

sentences.zh: 上遣李重進將兵趣廬州。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Li Chongjin with troops toward Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Li Chongjin with troops toward Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 唐主聞上在江上，恐遂南渡，又恥降號稱籓，乃遣兵部侍郎陳覺奉表，請傳位於太子弘冀，使聽命於中國。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler heard that the emperor was on the river, feared he would cross south, and was also ashamed to lower his title and call himself a vassal; he therefore sent Ministry of War vice minister Chen Jue with a memorial asking to pass the throne to Crown Prince Hongji and to take orders from the Central Court.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler, hearing that the emperor was on the Yangtze, feared a crossing south and was ashamed to demote himself to vassal status; he sent Ministry of War vice minister Chen Jue with a memorial offering to abdicate in favor of Crown Prince Hongji and submit to the Central Court.

sentences.zh: 時淮南惟廬、舒、蘄、黃未下。

translations.literal: At the time in Huainan only Lu, Shu, Qi, and Huang had not yet fallen.
translations.idiomatic: At the time in Huainan only Lu, Shu, Qi, and Huang prefectures still held out.

sentences.zh: 丙申，覺至迎鑾，見周兵之盛，白上，請遣人度江取表，獻四州之地，畫江為境，以求息兵，辭指甚哀。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Jue reached Yingluan, saw the strength of Zhou troops, reported to the emperor, and asked to send someone across the river to fetch the memorial, offering the four prefectures and taking the river as the border to seek a halt to arms; his words were very plaintive.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Jue reached Yingluan, saw how strong the Zhou forces were, and told the emperor he wished to send someone across the river for the formal memorial, offering the four prefectures and the Yangtze as the new border to halt the war; his plea was deeply sorrowful.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕本興師止取江北，今爾主能舉國內附，朕復何求！」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I raised the army only to take the north of the river; now if your ruler can bring the whole state to submit, what more do I seek!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I raised this army only to take the north bank; if your ruler will bring the whole realm to submit, what more could I want!"

sentences.zh: 覺拜謝而退。

translations.literal: Jue bowed in thanks and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Jue bowed in thanks and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，覺請遣其屬閤門承旨劉承遇如金陵，上賜唐主書，稱「皇帝恭問江南國主」，慰納之。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Jue asked to send his subordinate Gate Attendant-in-Ordinary Liu Chengyu to Jinling; the emperor bestowed a letter on the Tang ruler, styled "The Emperor respectfully inquires after the Jiangnan State Lord," and comfortingly accepted him.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Jue asked to send his subordinate Gate Attendant-in-Ordinary Liu Chengyu to Jinling; the emperor sent a letter to the Southern Tang ruler addressed "The Emperor respectfully inquires after the Lord of Jiangnan" and graciously accepted the submission.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，吳越奏遣上直都指揮使、處州刺史邵可遷、秀州刺史路彥銖以戰艦四百艘、士卒萬七千人屯通州南岸。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Wu-Yue reported dispatching Inner-Palace Commander-in-Chief and Chuzhou prefect Shao Keqian and Xiuzhou prefect Lu Yanzhen with four hundred warships and seventeen thousand troops to encamp on the south bank of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Wu-Yue reported that Inner-Palace Commander-in-Chief and Chuzhou prefect Shao Keqian and Xiuzhou prefect Lu Yanzhen had been sent with four hundred warships and seventeen thousand troops to encamp on the south bank opposite Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 唐主復遣劉承遇奉表稱唐國主，請獻江北四州，歲輸貢物數十萬。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler again sent Liu Chengyu with a memorial styling himself Lord of the Tang State, asking to offer the four north-of-river prefectures and to deliver several hundred thousand in annual tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler again sent Liu Chengyu with a memorial styling himself Lord of Tang, offering the four north-bank prefectures and promising annual tribute worth several hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 於是江北悉平，得州十四，縣六十。

translations.literal: Thereupon the north of the river was entirely pacified; fourteen prefectures and sixty counties were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the entire north bank was pacified; Zhou gained fourteen prefectures and sixty counties.

sentences.zh: 庚子，上賜唐主書，諭以：「緣江諸軍及兩浙、湖南、荊南兵並當罷歸，其廬、蘄、黃三道，亦令斂兵近外。

translations.literal: On gengzi, the emperor bestowed a letter on the Tang ruler, instructing him: "The armies along the river and the troops of the Two Zhes, Hunan, and Jingnan should all be dismissed and sent home; for the Lu, Qi, and Huang circuits as well, order the troops withdrawn to the near exterior.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, the emperor sent the Southern Tang ruler a letter instructing him: "All armies along the river and the forces from the Two Zhes, Hunan, and Jingnan are to be sent home; for Lu, Qi, and Huang as well, withdraw your troops to the near frontier.

sentences.zh: 俟彼將士及家屬皆就道，可遣人召將校以城邑付之。

translations.literal: When their officers and soldiers and families are all on the road, you may send someone to summon the commanders and hand over the cities and towns to them.
translations.idiomatic: When their officers, soldiers, and families are all on the road, you may send envoys to summon the commanders and hand the cities over to them.

sentences.zh: 江中舟艦有須往來者，並令就北岸引之。」

translations.literal: Any ships on the river that must come and go are all to be guided to the north bank."
translations.idiomatic: Any ships that must travel the river are to be guided along the north bank."

sentences.zh: 辛丑，陳覺辭行，又賜唐主書，諭以不必傳位於子。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Chen Jue took leave to depart; the emperor again bestowed a letter on the Tang ruler, instructing him that he need not pass the throne to his son.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Chen Jue took his leave; the emperor again wrote the Southern Tang ruler telling him that abdication in favor of his son was unnecessary.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，上自迎鑾復如揚州。

translations.literal: On renyin, the emperor returned from Yingluan to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, the emperor returned from Yingluan to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，詔吳越、荊南軍又歸本道；

translations.literal: On guimao, an edict ordered the Wu-Yue and Jingnan armies to return to their home circuits;
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, an edict ordered the Wu-Yue and Jingnan armies to return to their home circuits;

sentences.zh: 賜錢弘俶犒軍帛三萬匹，高保融一萬匹。

translations.literal: Qian Hongchu was granted thirty thousand bolts of silk to reward the army, and Gao Baorong ten thousand bolts.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Hongchu was granted thirty thousand bolts of silk to reward his troops, and Gao Baorong ten thousand bolts.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，置保信軍於廬州，以右龍武統軍趙匡贊為節度使。

translations.literal: On jiachen, the Baoxin Army was established at Luzhou, with Right Dragon Martial army commander Zhao Kuangzan as military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, the Baoxin Army was established at Luzhou with Right Dragon Martial army commander Zhao Kuangzan as its military governor.

sentences.zh: 丙午，唐主遣馮延己獻銀、絹、錢、茶、穀共百萬以犒軍。

translations.literal: On bingwu, the Tang ruler sent Feng Yanji to present silver, silk, cash, tea, and grain totaling a million to reward the army.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, the Southern Tang ruler sent Feng Yanji with silver, silk, cash, tea, and grain worth a million in total to reward the Zhou army.

sentences.zh: 己酉，命宋延渥將水軍三千溯江巡警。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Song Yanwo was ordered to lead three thousand naval troops upriver on patrol.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Song Yanwo was ordered to lead three thousand naval troops upriver on patrol.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，敕故淮南節度使楊行密、故升府節度使徐溫等墓並量給守戶。

translations.literal: On gengxu, an edict ordered that the tombs of the former Huainan military governor Yang Xingmi, the former Shengfu military governor Xu Wen, and others be each granted tomb-guard households as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, an edict ordered appropriate tomb-guard households assigned to the graves of former Huainan military governor Yang Xingmi, former Shengfu military governor Xu Wen, and others.

sentences.zh: 其江南群臣墓在江北者，亦委長吏以時檢校。

translations.literal: The tombs of Jiangnan ministers north of the river were also entrusted to local officials for timely inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Tombs of Jiangnan ministers lying north of the river were likewise entrusted to local officials for regular upkeep.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，唐主遣其臨汝公徐遼代己來上壽。

translations.literal: On xinhai, the Tang ruler sent his Duke of Linru Xu Liao in his stead to offer birthday felicitations.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, the Southern Tang ruler sent Duke of Linru Xu Liao in his place to offer birthday felicitations to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 是月，浚汴口，導河流達於淮，於是江、淮舟楫始通。

translations.literal: That month the Bian estuary was dredged and the river's flow guided to reach the Huai; thereby Yangtze and Huai shipping was opened for the first time.
translations.idiomatic: That month workers dredged the Bian estuary and channeled the Yellow River to the Huai, opening river traffic between the Yangtze and Huai basins for the first time.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙卯，帝自揚州北還。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on yimao, the emperor returned north from Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on yimao, Emperor Shizong marched north from Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 新作太廟成。

translations.literal: The newly built Imperial Ancestral Temple was completed.
translations.idiomatic: The newly built Imperial Ancestral Temple was completed.

sentences.zh: 庚申，神主入廟。

translations.literal: On gengshen, the spirit tablets entered the temple.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, the imperial spirit tablets were installed in the temple.

sentences.zh: 辛酉夜，錢唐城南火，延及內城，官府廬舍幾盡。

translations.literal: On the night of xinyou, fire broke out south of Qiantang city, spread to the inner city, and nearly all government offices and dwellings were consumed.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of xinyou, fire broke out south of Qiantang and spread into the inner city, destroying nearly all government offices and dwellings.

sentences.zh: 壬戌旦，火將及鎮國倉。

translations.literal: At dawn on renxu, the fire was about to reach the Zhenguo granary.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on renxu, the flames were about to reach the Zhenguo state granary.

sentences.zh: 吳越王弘俶久疾，自強出救火。

translations.literal: Wu-Yue king Hongchu had long been ill but forced himself out to fight the fire.
translations.idiomatic: Wu-Yue king Qian Hongchu had long been ill but forced himself out to fight the fire.

sentences.zh: 火止，謂左右曰：「吾疾因災而愈。」

translations.literal: When the fire stopped, he said to those around him, "My illness has been cured by this calamity."
translations.idiomatic: When the fire died out, he told his attendants, "This disaster has cured my illness."

sentences.zh: 眾心稍安。

translations.literal: The people's hearts were somewhat reassured.
translations.idiomatic: The people's spirits were somewhat reassured.

sentences.zh: 帝之南征也，契丹乘虛入寇。

translations.literal: While the emperor was on the southern campaign, the Khitan took advantage of the opening to invade.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Shizong was on the southern campaign, the Khitan seized the opportunity to raid the border.

sentences.zh: 壬申，帝至大梁，命鎮寧節度使張永德將兵備御北邊。

translations.literal: On renshen, the emperor reached Daliang and ordered Zhenning military governor Zhang Yongde to lead troops to guard against the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Emperor Shizong reached Daliang and ordered Zhenning military governor Zhang Yongde to lead troops in defense of the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 五月，辛巳朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the xinsi new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the xinsi new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 詔賞勞南征士卒及淮南新附之民。

translations.literal: An edict rewarded and comforted the troops of the southern campaign and the newly submitted people of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict rewarded the troops of the southern campaign and the newly submitted people of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以太祖皇帝領忠武節度使，徙安審琦為平盧節度使。

translations.literal: On xinmao, the Taizu emperor was made to hold the Zhongwu military governorship, and An Shenqi was transferred to Pinglu military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, the late Taizu emperor's post as Zhongwu military governor was filled by appointment, and An Shenqi was transferred to Pinglu military governor.

sentences.zh: 成德節度使郭崇攻契丹東城，拔之，以報其入寇也。

translations.literal: Chengde military governor Guo Chong attacked the Khitan eastern city, took it, in reprisal for their invasion.
translations.idiomatic: Chengde military governor Guo Chong attacked the Khitan eastern city, captured it, and thereby repaid their raid.

sentences.zh: 唐主避周諱，更名景，下令去帝號，稱國主，凡天子儀制皆有降損，去年號，用周正朔，仍告於太廟。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler avoided Zhou taboo names, changed his name to Jing, ordered removal of the imperial title and styled himself State Lord; all Son of Heaven ritual and institutions were reduced, the era name was dropped, Zhou's calendar was adopted, and this was still announced at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler avoided Zhou taboo names, changed his name to Jing, renounced the imperial title in favor of State Lord, reduced all imperial ritual to vassal scale, dropped his era name, adopted Zhou's calendar, and reported the change at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 左僕射、同平章事馮延己罷為太子太傅，門下侍郎、同平章事嚴續罷為少傅、樞密使，兵部侍郎陳覺罷守本官。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Co-Equal to the Three Dukes Feng Yanji was dismissed to Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince; Vice Director of the Chancellery and Co-Equal Yan Xu was dismissed to Junior Mentor and Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Ministry of War vice minister Chen Jue was dismissed to retain his original office only.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Feng Yanji was demoted to Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince; Vice Director of the Chancellery Yan Xu was demoted to Junior Mentor and Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Ministry of War vice minister Chen Jue was stripped of his concurrent posts and left with his original office only.

sentences.zh: 初，馮延己以取中原之策說唐主，由是有寵。

translations.literal: Earlier Feng Yanji had urged on the Tang ruler a strategy to seize the Central Plains, and thereby won favor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Feng Yanji had persuaded the Southern Tang ruler with a plan to seize the Central Plains, and thereby won his favor.

sentences.zh: 延己嘗笑烈祖戢兵為齷齪，曰：「安陸所喪才數千兵，為之輟食咨嗟者旬日，此田舍翁識量耳，安足與成大事！

translations.literal: Yanji once mocked the Founding Emperor's restraint of arms as petty, saying, "At Anlu he lost only a few thousand troops, yet for it he stopped eating and sighed for ten days—this is the outlook of a rustic, how could he accomplish great things!
translations.idiomatic: Yanji had mocked the founding emperor's restraint in war as petty, saying, "He lost only a few thousand men at Anlu yet went without proper meals and sighed over it for ten days—that is a peasant's outlook, unfit for great undertakings!

sentences.zh: 豈如今上暴師數萬於外，而擊球宴樂無異平日，真英主也！」

translations.literal: How unlike the present sovereign, who exposes tens of thousands of troops abroad yet plays ball and feasts as on ordinary days—truly an heroic ruler!"
translations.idiomatic: How unlike our present sovereign, who keeps tens of thousands in the field yet plays polo and feasts as on any ordinary day—a true heroic ruler!"

sentences.zh: 延己與其黨談論，常以天下為己任，更相唱和。

translations.literal: Yanji and his faction in discussion constantly took the empire as their own charge, echoing one another.
translations.idiomatic: Yanji and his faction constantly spoke as though the fate of the empire rested on them, echoing one another's boasts.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士常夢錫屢言延己等浮誕，不可信，唐主不聽。

translations.literal: Hanlin academician Chang Mengxi repeatedly said that Yanji and the rest were inflated and reckless and not to be trusted; the Tang ruler would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academician Chang Mengxi repeatedly warned that Yanji and his circle were reckless braggarts unworthy of trust; the Southern Tang ruler would not listen.

sentences.zh: 夢錫曰：「奸言似忠，陛下不悟，國必亡矣！」

translations.literal: Mengxi said, "Treacherous words resemble loyal ones; if Your Majesty does not perceive this, the state will surely perish!"
translations.idiomatic: Mengxi said, "Treacherous counsel wears the mask of loyalty; if Your Majesty does not see through it, the state is doomed!"

sentences.zh: 及臣服於周，延己之黨相與言，有謂周為大朝者，夢錫大笑曰：「諸公常欲致君堯、舜，何意今日自為小朝邪！」

translations.literal: When they submitted to Zhou, Yanji's faction spoke among themselves, some calling Zhou the great court; Mengxi laughed loudly and said, "You gentlemen always wished to make the ruler a Yao or Shun—why today do you make yourselves a petty court!"
translations.idiomatic: After submission to Zhou, Yanji's faction spoke among themselves, some calling Zhou the great court; Mengxi laughed aloud and said, "You always talked of making our ruler another Yao or Shun—why do you now make yourselves subjects of a petty court!"

sentences.zh: 眾默然。

translations.literal: The company fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: The company fell silent.

sentences.zh: 自唐主內附，帝止因其使者賜書，未嘗遣使至其國。

translations.literal: Since the Tang ruler submitted internally, the emperor only bestowed letters through his envoys and had never sent envoys to his state.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Southern Tang ruler submitted, the emperor had communicated only through Tang envoys and had not yet sent an embassy to Jinling.

sentences.zh: 己酉，始命太僕卿馮延魯、衛尉少卿鍾謨使於唐，賜以御衣、玉帶等及犒軍帛十萬，並今年《欽天歷》。

translations.literal: On jiyou, he first ordered Grand Master of the Stud Feng Yanlu and Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Regalia Zhong Mo as envoys to Tang, granting imperial robes, jade belts, and the like, one hundred thousand bolts of silk to reward the army, and this year's Qintian Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, he first dispatched Grand Master of the Stud Feng Yanlu and Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Regalia Zhong Mo as envoys to Southern Tang, bestowing imperial robes, jade belts, one hundred thousand bolts of silk to reward the army, and the current year's Qintian Calendar.

sentences.zh: 劉承遇之還自金陵也，唐主使陳覺白帝，以江南無鹵田，願得海陵鹽監南屬以贍軍。

translations.literal: When Liu Chengyu returned from Jinling, the Tang ruler had Chen Jue inform the emperor that Jiangnan had no salt pans and he wished the southern portion of the Hailing salt commission to be attached to him to support the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Chengyu returned from Jinling, the Southern Tang ruler had Chen Jue tell the emperor that Jiangnan lacked salt fields and asked that the southern portion of the Hailing salt commission be assigned to Tang to support his troops.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「海陵在江北，難以交居，當別有處分。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Hailing is north of the river; joint residence would be difficult; there will be separate arrangements."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Hailing lies north of the river and cannot be shared; we will make other arrangements."

sentences.zh: 至是，詔歲支鹽三十萬斛以給江南，所俘獲江南士卒，稍稍歸之。

translations.literal: By this time an edict ordered three hundred thousand hu of salt supplied annually to Jiangnan, and captured Jiangnan soldiers were gradually returned.
translations.idiomatic: By then an edict ordered three hundred thousand hu of salt supplied annually to Jiangnan, and captured Southern Tang soldiers were gradually sent home.

sentences.zh: 六月，壬子，昭義節度使李筠奏擊北漢石會關，拔其六寨。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on renzi, Zhaoyi military governor Li Yun reported attacking Northern Han's Shihui Pass and taking six stockades.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renzi, Zhaoyi military governor Li Yun reported attacking Northern Han's Shihui Pass and capturing six stockades.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，晉州奏都監李謙溥擊北漢，破孝義。

translations.literal: On yimao, Jin Prefecture reported that the superintendent Li Qianpu attacked Northern Han and defeated Xiaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Jin Prefecture reported that Superintendent Li Qianpu had attacked Northern Han and captured Xiaoyi.

sentences.zh: 高保融遣使勸蜀主稱籓於周，蜀主報以前歲遣胡立致書於周而不答。

translations.literal: Gao Baorong sent envoys to urge the Shu ruler to submit as a vassal to Zhou; the Shu ruler replied that in the previous year he had sent Hu Li to deliver a letter to Zhou, but received no answer.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Baorong sent envoys urging the ruler of Shu to submit to Zhou as a vassal. The Shu ruler replied that the year before he had dispatched Hu Li with a letter to Zhou, yet received no answer.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙戌，初行《大周刑統》。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingxu, the Great Zhou Penal Code was first put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingxu, the Great Zhou Penal Code took effect for the first time.

sentences.zh: 帝欲均田租，丁亥，以元稹《均田圖》遍賜諸道。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to equalize land rents; on dinghai, Yuan Zhen's Diagram of Equalized Fields was bestowed on all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong wished to equalize land rents. On dinghai he had Yuan Zhen's Diagram of Equalized Fields distributed to every circuit.

sentences.zh: 閏月，唐清源節度使兼中書令留從效遣牙將蔡仲贇衣商人服，以絹表置革帶中，間道來稱籓。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, Liu Congxiao, Southern Tang military governor of Qingyuan and concurrently Director of the Secretariat, sent his military officer Cai Zhongyun dressed as a merchant, with a silk petition placed inside his leather belt, to come by a secret route and submit allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, Southern Tang's Qingyuan military governor and concurrent Director of the Secretariat Liu Congxiao sent adjutant Cai Zhongyun disguised as a merchant, a silk petition hidden in his belt, along a back route to offer submission.

sentences.zh: 唐江西元帥晉王景遂之赴洪州也，以時方用兵，啟求大臣以自副，唐主以樞密副使、工部侍郎李征古為鎮南節度副使。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin, Jing Sui, Southern Tang military commander of Jiangxi, went to Hongzhou, because warfare was then underway he memorialized requesting a senior minister as his deputy; the Southern Tang ruler appointed Li Zhenggu, Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council and Vice Minister of Works, as deputy military governor of Zhennan.
translations.idiomatic: When Southern Tang's Jiangxi commander Prince of Jin Jing Sui set out for Hongzhou, active campaigning led him to request a senior minister as deputy. The Southern Tang ruler appointed Privy Council Vice Commissioner and Vice Minister of Works Li Zhenggu deputy military governor of Zhennan.

sentences.zh: 征古傲很專恣，景遂雖寬厚，久而不能堪，常欲斬征古，自拘於有司，左右諫而止，景遂忽忽不樂。

translations.literal: Zhenggu was arrogant, harsh, and willful; though Jing Sui was generous and tolerant, in time he could no longer bear it and often wished to execute Zhenggu and surrender himself to the authorities; his attendants remonstrated and stopped him, and Jing Sui grew despondent and unhappy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenggu was proud, cruel, and overbearing. Though Jing Sui was broad-minded by nature, he could not endure him forever; he repeatedly wanted to kill Zhenggu and turn himself over to the law. His attendants dissuaded him, and Jing Sui sank into gloom.

sentences.zh: 太子弘冀在東宮多不法，唐主怒，嘗以球杖擊之曰：「吾當復召景遂。」

translations.literal: Crown Prince Hongji in the Eastern Palace frequently acted unlawfully; the Southern Tang ruler, in anger, once struck him with a ball stick and said, "I ought to recall Jing Sui."
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Hongji committed many improprieties in the Eastern Palace. The Southern Tang ruler, furious, once beat him with a ball mallet and said, "I should recall Jing Sui."

sentences.zh: 昭慶宮使袁從范從景遂為洪州都押牙，或譖從范之子於景遂，景遂欲殺之，從范由是怨望。

translations.literal: Zhaoging Palace Commissioner Yuan Congfan had followed Jing Sui to serve as chief military adjutant at Hongzhou; someone slandered Congfan's son to Jing Sui, and Jing Sui wished to kill him, so Congfan came to harbor resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoging Palace Commissioner Yuan Congfan had accompanied Jing Sui to Hongzhou as chief military adjutant. Someone denounced Congfan's son to Jing Sui, who sought to kill the boy; Congfan therefore nursed a grievance.

sentences.zh: 弘冀聞之，密遣從范毒之。

translations.literal: When Hongji heard of this, he secretly sent Congfan to poison him.
translations.idiomatic: Hongji learned of this and secretly dispatched Congfan to poison Jing Sui.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚辰，景遂擊球渴甚，從范進漿，景遂飲之而卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on gengchen, Jing Sui was extremely thirsty after playing ball; Congfan offered him a drink, and Jing Sui drank it and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on gengchen, Jing Sui was parched after a game of cuju. Congfan brought him a drink; Jing Sui drank it and died.

sentences.zh: 未殯，體已潰。

translations.literal: Before the body was encoffined, the corpse had already putrefied.
translations.idiomatic: Even before the funeral rites began, the body had already decomposed.

sentences.zh: 唐主不之知，贈皇太弟，謚曰文成。

translations.literal: The Southern Tang ruler did not know of this; he posthumously enfeoffed him as Imperial Younger Brother and gave him the posthumous title Wen Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler knew nothing of the affair. He posthumously honored Jing Sui as Imperial Younger Brother with the posthumous name Wen Cheng.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，南漢中宗殂，長子衛王繼興即帝位，更名鋹，改元大寶。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Mid-Emperor of Southern Han died; his eldest son, Prince of Wei Jixing, ascended the throne, changed his name to Chang, and adopted the era name Dabao.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Mid-Emperor of Southern Han died. His eldest son Prince of Wei Jixing took the throne, changed his name to Chang, and proclaimed the era name Dabao.

sentences.zh: 鋹年十六，國事皆決於宦官玉清宮使龔澄樞及女侍中盧瓊仙等，台省官備位而已。

translations.literal: Chang was sixteen years old; all state affairs were decided by the eunuch Jade Purity Palace Commissioner Gong Chenshu and Lady Attendant-in-Chief Lu Qiongxian and others, while officials of the central administration held office in name only.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was only sixteen. State affairs were decided by eunuch Jade Purity Palace Commissioner Gong Chenshu, Lady Attendant-in-Chief Lu Qiongxian, and their circle; central government officials were mere figureheads.

sentences.zh: 甲申，唐始置進奏院於大梁。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Southern Tang first established a memorial-report office at Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Southern Tang established a memorial-report office at Daliang for the first time.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，命西上閣門使靈壽曹彬使於吳越，賜吳越王弘俶騎軍鋼甲二百，步軍甲五千及他兵器。

translations.literal: On renchen, the emperor ordered Xishang Gemen Commissioner Cao Bin of Lingshou to serve as envoy to Wu-Yue, bestowing on King of Wu-Yue Hong Chu two hundred suits of steel armor for cavalry, five thousand suits of infantry armor, and other weapons.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Emperor Shizong appointed Xishang Gemen Commissioner Cao Bin of Lingshou envoy to Wu-Yue, granting King Qian Hongchu two hundred suits of cavalry steel armor, five thousand suits of infantry armor, and other arms.

sentences.zh: 彬事畢亟返，不受饋遺，吳越人以輕舟追與之，至於數四，彬曰：「吾終不受，是竊名也。

translations.literal: When Bin finished his mission he hurried back and would accept no gifts; the people of Wu-Yue pursued him in light boats to offer them, as many as four times, and Bin said, "I will never accept them—that would be stealing a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Bin completed his mission and returned at once, refusing all presents. The people of Wu-Yue chased him in swift boats to press gifts upon him, as many as four times. Bin said, "I will never accept them; to do so would be to steal credit for virtue.

sentences.zh: 盡籍其數，歸而獻之。

translations.literal: He fully recorded their number and, upon returning, presented the list.
translations.idiomatic: He recorded every item in full and, on his return, submitted the inventory to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「曏之奉使者，乞丐無厭，使四方輕朝命，卿能如是，甚善。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Former envoys sent on mission were insatiable beggars, causing the four quarters to look lightly on imperial orders; that you were able to act thus is very good.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Envoys of old were shameless beggars, and the realm came to hold the court's commands in contempt. That you conducted yourself as you did is excellent.

sentences.zh: 然彼以遺卿，卿自取之。」

translations.literal: Yet since they gave them to you, take them for yourself."
translations.idiomatic: But since they were given to you, you may keep them."

sentences.zh: 彬始拜受，悉以散於親識，家無留者。

translations.literal: Only then did Bin bow and accept, and he distributed everything among relatives and acquaintances, keeping none at home.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Bin bow and accept the gifts, then gave them all away to relatives and friends, leaving nothing in his household.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，馮延魯、鍾謨來自唐，唐主手表謝恩，其略曰：「天地之恩厚矣，父母之恩深矣，子不謝父，人何報天！

translations.literal: On xinchou, Feng Yanlu and Zhong Mo came from Southern Tang; the Southern Tang ruler wrote by hand to express gratitude, in summary saying, "The grace of Heaven and Earth is profound; the kindness of parents runs deep. If a child does not thank his father, how can a person repay Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Feng Yanlu and Zhong Mo arrived from Southern Tang. The Southern Tang ruler wrote a personal letter of thanks, saying in part, "The bounty of Heaven and Earth is vast; a parent's love runs deep. If a son does not thank his father, how can a man repay Heaven!

sentences.zh: 惟有赤心，可酬大造。

translations.literal: Only with a loyal heart can one requite such great kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Only a loyal heart can repay such boundless grace.

sentences.zh: 「又乞比籓方，賜詔書。

translations.literal: " He also requested that, like other vassal regions, an imperial edict be granted.
translations.idiomatic: " He also asked that, as with other submitted regions, an imperial edict be issued.

sentences.zh: 又稱：「有情事令鐘謨上奏，乞令早還。」

translations.literal: He also stated, "There is a matter I wish Zhong Mo to report; I beg that he be allowed to return soon."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "There is a matter I wish Zhong Mo to report in person; please allow him to return at once."

sentences.zh: 唐主復令謨白帝，欲傳位太子。

translations.literal: The Southern Tang ruler again had Mo inform the emperor that he wished to abdicate in favor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler also instructed Mo to tell the emperor that he wished to transfer the throne to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 九月，丁巳，以延魯為刑部侍郎、謨為給事中。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on dingsi, Yanlu was appointed Vice Minister of Justice and Mo was appointed Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on dingsi, Feng Yanlu was appointed Vice Minister of Justice and Zhong Mo Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 己未，先遣謨還，賜書諭以「未可傳位」之意。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Mo was sent back first, and an imperial letter was bestowed explaining that abdication was not yet permissible.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Zhong Mo was sent home first, with an imperial letter explaining that the throne could not yet be transferred.

sentences.zh: 唐主復遣吏部尚書、知樞密院殷崇義來賀天清節。

translations.literal: The Southern Tang ruler again sent Yin Chongyi, Minister of Personnel and overseer of the Privy Council, to congratulate him on the Tianqing Festival.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler again dispatched Minister of Personnel and Privy Council overseer Yin Chongyi to offer congratulations on the Tianqing Festival.

sentences.zh: 帝謀伐蜀，冬，十月，己卯，以戶部侍郎高防為西南面水陸制置使，右贊善大夫李玉為判官。

translations.literal: The emperor planned to attack Shu; in winter, the tenth month, on jimao, Gao Fang, Vice Minister of Revenue, was appointed Southwest Land-and-Water Military Commissioner, and Li Yu, Right Advisor, was appointed his aide.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong planned an expedition against Shu. In winter, the tenth month, on jimao, he appointed Vice Minister of Revenue Gao Fang Southwest Land-and-Water Military Commissioner, with Right Advisor Li Yu as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 甲午，帝歸馮延魯及左監門衛上將軍許文稹、右千牛衛上將軍邊鎬、衛尉卿周廷構於唐。

translations.literal: On jiawu, the emperor returned Feng Yanlu, Left Gate Guard General Xu Wenzhen, Right Thousand-Ox Guard General Bian Hao, and Chamberlain Zhou Tinggou to Southern Tang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, the emperor sent Feng Yanlu, Left Gate Guard General Xu Wenzhen, Right Thousand-Ox Guard General Bian Hao, and Chamberlain Zhou Tinggou back to Southern Tang.

sentences.zh: 唐主以文稹等皆敗軍之俘，棄不復用。

translations.literal: The Southern Tang ruler regarded Wenzhen and the others as captives from defeated armies and cast them aside without re-employing them.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler considered Xu Wenzhen and the others prisoners from broken armies and abandoned them without further appointment.

sentences.zh: 高保融再遺蜀主書，勸稱臣於周，蜀主集將相議之，李昊曰：「從之則君父之辱，違之則周師必至，諸將能拒周乎？」

translations.literal: Gao Baorong again sent a letter to the Shu ruler urging submission to Zhou as a vassal; the Shu ruler gathered his generals and ministers to discuss it, and Li Hao said, "If we comply, it is shame to sovereign and father; if we defy, Zhou armies will surely come—can our generals resist Zhou?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Baorong again wrote the Shu ruler urging him to submit to Zhou. The Shu ruler convened his generals and ministers to deliberate. Li Hao said, "To obey is to disgrace both ruler and father; to refuse is to invite Zhou's armies. Can our commanders hold Zhou back?"

sentences.zh: 諸將皆曰：「以陛下聖明，江山險固，豈可望風屈服！

translations.literal: All the generals said, "With Your Majesty's sagely brilliance and our rivers and mountains fortified by nature, how could we submit at the mere rumor of their approach!
translations.idiomatic: The generals all replied, "With Your Majesty's wisdom and our natural defenses, how could we bow at the first wind of invasion!

sentences.zh: 秣馬厲兵，正為今日。

translations.literal: We have fed our horses and sharpened our weapons precisely for this day.
translations.idiomatic: We have fed the horses and honed the blades for just such a day.

sentences.zh: 臣等請以死衛社稷！」

translations.literal: We request to defend the altars of state with our lives!"
translations.idiomatic: We ask only to die defending the realm!"

sentences.zh: 丁酉，蜀主命昊草書，極言拒絕之。

translations.literal: On dingyou, the Shu ruler ordered Hao to draft a letter vehemently refusing.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, the Shu ruler ordered Li Hao to draft a reply that refused in the strongest terms.

sentences.zh: 詔左散騎常侍須城艾穎等三十四人分行諸州，均定田租。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Left Regular Attendant Ai Ying of Xucheng and thirty-four others to divide among the prefectures to assess and fix land rents.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dispatched Left Regular Attendant Ai Ying of Xucheng and thirty-four others to tour the prefectures and equalize land rents.

sentences.zh: 庚子，詔諸州並鄉村，率以百戶為團，團置耆長三人。

translations.literal: On gengzi, an edict ordered that in all prefectures, including villages, generally every hundred households form a tuan, with three elders appointed per tuan.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, an edict decreed that throughout the prefectures and countryside, every hundred households were to form a tuan, each tuan to have three elders.

sentences.zh: 帝留心農事，刻木為耕夫、蠶婦，置之殿庭。

translations.literal: The emperor attended to agricultural affairs, carving wooden figures of plowmen and silk-reeling women and placing them in the palace hall.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong kept farming close to heart; he had wooden figures of a plowman and a silk-reeling woman carved and set up in the palace hall.

sentences.zh: 命武勝節度使宋延渥以水軍巡江。

translations.literal: He ordered Song Yanwo, military governor of Wusheng, to patrol the river with a naval force.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Wusheng military governor Song Yanwo to patrol the river with a fleet.

sentences.zh: 高保融奏，聞王師將伐蜀，請以水軍趣三峽，詔褒之。

translations.literal: Gao Baorong memorialized that he had heard the imperial army would attack Shu and requested to lead his naval force toward the Three Gorges; an edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Baorong reported that he had learned the imperial army was about to strike Shu and asked to advance his fleet toward the Three Gorges. An edict commended him.

sentences.zh: 十一月，庚戌，敕竇儼編集《大周通禮》、《大周正樂》。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on gengxu, Dou Yan was ordered to compile the Grand Zhou Comprehensive Rites and Grand Zhou Correct Music.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on gengxu, Dou Yan was commanded to compile the Grand Zhou Comprehensive Rites and Grand Zhou Correct Music.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，南漢葬文武光明孝皇帝於昭陵，廟號中宗。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Southern Han buried Emperor Wen Wu Guang Ming Xiao at Zhaoling, with temple name Zhongzong.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Southern Han interred Emperor Wen Wu Guang Ming Xiao at Zhaoling, with the temple name Zhongzong.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，唐主復遣禮部侍郎鐘謨入見。

translations.literal: On yichou, the Southern Tang ruler again sent Zhong Mo, Vice Minister of Rites, to have an audience.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, the Southern Tang ruler again sent Vice Minister of Rites Zhong Mo to audience with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 李玉至長安，或言「蜀歸安鎮在長安南三百餘里，可襲取也。」

translations.literal: When Li Yu reached Chang'an, someone said, "Shu's Gui'an garrison lies more than three hundred li south of Chang'an and can be taken by surprise."
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yu arrived at Chang'an, someone said, "Shu's Gui'an garrison lies over three hundred li south of Chang'an and could be seized in a sudden strike."

sentences.zh: 玉信之，牒永興節度使王彥超，索兵二百，彥超以為歸安道阻隘難取，玉曰：「吾自奉密旨。」

translations.literal: Yu believed it and dispatched a message to Wang Yanchao, military governor of Yongxing, requesting two hundred troops; Yanchao thought the route to Gui'an was narrow and difficult and hard to take, and Yu said, "I myself carry secret orders."
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu believed this and wrote to Yongxing military governor Wang Yanchao demanding two hundred men. Yanchao argued that the road to Gui'an was narrow and treacherous and the place hard to seize. Yu replied, "I act on secret imperial orders."

sentences.zh: 彥超不得已與之。

translations.literal: Yanchao had no choice but to give them to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanchao had no choice but to provide the troops.

sentences.zh: 玉將以往，十二月，蜀歸安鎮遏使李承勳據險邀之，斬玉，其眾皆沒。

translations.literal: Yu was about to set out. In the twelfth month, Li Chengxun, the Gui'an Suppression Commissioner of Shu, waylaid him at a defensible pass, beheaded Yu, and his entire force was wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu was about to march when, in the twelfth month, Li Chengxun, Later Shu's Gui'an Suppression Commissioner, ambushed him at a narrow defile, cut off his head, and annihilated his entire command.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，蜀主以右衛聖步軍都指使趙崇韜為北面招討使，丙戌，以奉鑾肅衛都指揮使、武信節度使兼中書令孟貽業為昭武、文州都招討使，左衛聖馬軍都指揮使趙思進為東面招討使，山南西道節度使韓保貞為北面都招討使，將兵六萬，分屯要害以備周。

translations.literal: On yiyou, the Shu ruler appointed Zhao Chongtao, Right Guard Sacred Foot Army Director, Northern Pacification Commissioner; on bingxu, he appointed Meng Yiye, Sacred Escort Guard Commander-in-Chief and Wuxin military governor concurrent Central Secretariat Director, Grand Pacification Commissioner of Zhaowu and Wen Prefectures; Zhao Sijin, Left Guard Sacred Horse Army Commander-in-Chief, Eastern Pacification Commissioner; and Han Baozhen, Shannan West Circuit military governor, Grand Northern Pacification Commissioner—sixty thousand troops in all, garrisoned at key points to guard against Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, the Later Shu ruler made Zhao Chongtao, director of the Right Guard Sacred Foot Army, Northern Pacification Commissioner. On bingxu he appointed Meng Yiye—Sacred Escort Guard commander-in-chief, Wuxin military governor, and concurrent Central Secretariat director—Grand Pacification Commissioner for Zhaowu and Wen; Zhao Sijin, commander of the Left Guard Sacred Horse Army, Eastern Pacification Commissioner; and Han Baozhen, military governor of Shannan West Circuit, Grand Northern Pacification Commissioner. Sixty thousand men were deployed to hold the critical passes against Later Zhou.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，詔凡諸色課戶及俸戶並勒歸州縣，其幕職、州縣官自今並支俸錢及米麥。

translations.literal: On bingxu, an edict: all categories of tax households and salary households alike were compelled to return to county jurisdiction; from now on, staff officers and county and prefecture officials were all to be paid salaries in cash and in grain.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Emperor Shizong issued an edict: every category of tax household and salary household was to be registered once more under county authority, and from that day forward all staff officers and local officials were to receive their pay in cash, grain, and wheat.

sentences.zh: 初，唐太傅兼中書令楚公宋齊丘多樹朋黨，欲以專固朝權，躁進之士爭附之，推獎以為國之元老。

translations.literal: Previously, Song Qiqiu, Grand Tutor of Tang, concurrent Central Secretariat Director, Duke of Chu, had cultivated many factions, seeking thereby to monopolize court power; men eager for advancement competed to attach themselves to him, extolling him as the state's elder statesman.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Southern Tang's Grand Tutor and concurrent Central Secretariat Director, Duke of Chu Song Qiqiu, had built up a wide network of partisans to seize and hold court power for himself. Ambitious men clamored to join his circle and hailed him as the nation's elder pillar.

sentences.zh: 樞密使陳覺、副使李征古恃齊丘之勢，尤驕慢。

translations.literal: Privy Counselor Chen Jue and Vice Counselor Li Zhenggu, relying on Qiqiu's power, were especially arrogant and insolent.
translations.idiomatic: Privy Counselor Chen Jue and Vice Counselor Li Zhenggu, leaning on Qiqiu's influence, were more arrogant and overbearing than anyone.

sentences.zh: 及許文稹等敗於紫金山，覺與齊丘、景達自濠州遁歸，國人忷懼。

translations.literal: When Xu Wenzhen and others were defeated at Purple Gold Mountain, Jue together with Qiqiu and Jing Da fled back from Haozhou; the people were alarmed and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: After Xu Wenzhen and the others were routed at Purple Gold Mountain, Chen Jue fled back from Haozhou with Song Qiqiu and Jing Da, and throughout the realm fear spread.

sentences.zh: 唐主嘗歎曰：「吾國家一朝至此！」

translations.literal: The Tang ruler once sighed and said, "Our state has come to this in a single morning!
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler once sighed and said, "Our kingdom has fallen to this in a single morning!

sentences.zh: 因泣下。

translations.literal: He wept.
translations.idiomatic: He burst into tears.

sentences.zh: 征古曰：「陛下當治兵以扞敵，涕泣何為！

translations.literal: Zhenggu said, "Your Majesty ought to ready troops to repel the enemy—what use are tears!
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhenggu said, "Your Majesty should drill the army and meet the enemy—what good are tears!

sentences.zh: 豈飲酒過量邪，將乳母不至邪？」

translations.literal: Have you drunk too much, or is your wet nurse not here?"
translations.idiomatic: Have you drunk yourself senseless, or has your wet nurse failed to arrive?"

sentences.zh: 唐主色變，而征古舉止自若。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler's countenance changed, but Zhenggu remained entirely at ease in his bearing.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler's face darkened, but Li Zhenggu carried on as calmly as if nothing had happened.

sentences.zh: 會司天奏：「天文有變，人主宜避位禳災。」

translations.literal: Just then the Directorate of Astronomy reported, "There are changes in the heavens; the ruler ought to abdicate the throne to avert calamity."
translations.idiomatic: At that moment the Directorate of Astronomy reported, "The heavens show ominous signs; the sovereign should step aside from the throne to avert disaster."

sentences.zh: 唐主乃曰：「禍難方殷，吾欲釋去萬機，棲心沖寂，誰可以托國者？」

translations.literal: The Tang ruler then said, "Disaster presses close; I wish to relinquish the myriad affairs of state and settle my heart in quiet emptiness—who can I entrust the realm to?"
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler then said, "Catastrophe is upon us. I wish to lay down the myriad burdens of rule and dwell in quiet emptiness of heart—whom can I entrust with the kingdom?"

sentences.zh: 征古曰：「宋公，造國手也，陛下如厭萬機，何不舉國授之！」

translations.literal: Zhenggu said, "Lord Song is the maker of the state; if Your Majesty tires of the myriad affairs, why not entrust the entire realm to him!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhenggu said, "Lord Song built this state with his own hands. If Your Majesty is weary of governing, why not hand the whole realm over to him!"

sentences.zh: 覺曰：「陛下深居禁中，國事皆委宋公，先行後聞，臣等時入侍，談釋、老而已。」

translations.literal: Jue said, "Your Majesty should dwell deep within the inner palace; all state affairs should be entrusted to Lord Song—act first, inform later. We would occasionally attend upon you and discuss only Buddhism and Daoism."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jue said, "Your Majesty should retire deep into the inner palace and leave all affairs of state to Lord Song—let him act first and report afterward. We would visit from time to time and speak only of Buddhist and Daoist teachings."

sentences.zh: 唐主心慍，即命中書舍人豫章陳喬草詔行之。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler was inwardly angry and immediately ordered Secretariat Drafter Chen Qiao of Yuzhang to draft an edict to carry this out.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler, seething within, at once ordered Secretariat Drafter Chen Qiao of Yuzhang to draft an edict putting the plan into effect.

sentences.zh: 喬惶恐請見，曰：「陛下一署此詔，臣不復得見矣！」

translations.literal: Qiao, in fear, requested an audience and said, "If Your Majesty signs this edict, I shall never see you again!
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qiao, terrified, begged for an audience and said, "If Your Majesty affixes your seal to this edict, I shall never stand before you again!

sentences.zh: 因極言其不可。

translations.literal: He spoke at length against its impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: He argued with all his force that it must not be done.

sentences.zh: 唐主笑曰：「爾亦知其非邪？」

translations.literal: The Tang ruler laughed and said, "So you too know it is wrong?
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler laughed and said, "So even you know this is wrong?

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: He stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 由是因晉王出鎮，以征古為之副，覺自周還，亦罷近職。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Prince of Jin was sent out to garrison a post; Zhenggu was made his deputy; Jue, upon returning from Zhou, was also removed from near duties.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Prince of Jin was sent out to take command of a garrison post, with Li Zhenggu as his deputy; Chen Jue, once he returned from Later Zhou, was likewise stripped of his posts at court.

sentences.zh: 鐘謨素與李德明善，以德明之死怨齊丘。

translations.literal: Zhong Mo had long been on good terms with Li Deming and, because of Deming's death, bore resentment against Qiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Mo had long been close to Li Deming, and after Deming's death he nursed a deep grudge against Song Qiqiu.

sentences.zh: 及奉使歸唐，言於唐主曰：「齊丘乘國之危，遽謀篡竊，陳覺、李征古為之羽翼，理不可容。」

translations.literal: When he returned on mission to Tang, he said to the Tang ruler, "Qiqiu, seizing the state's peril, hastily plotted usurpation; Chen Jue and Li Zhenggu were his wings—this cannot be tolerated."
translations.idiomatic: When he returned from his mission to Southern Tang, he told the ruler, "Song Qiqiu exploited the kingdom's crisis to plot a swift usurpation, with Chen Jue and Li Zhenggu as his wings. Such men cannot be allowed to remain."

sentences.zh: 陳覺之自周還，矯以帝命謂唐主曰：「聞江南連歲拒命，皆宰相嚴續之謀，當為我斬之。」

translations.literal: When Chen Jue returned from Zhou, he falsely invoked the emperor's command and told the Tang ruler, "I hear that Jiangnan's defiance of orders these many years was all the scheme of Chancellor Yan Xu—you should execute him for me."
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Jue returned from Later Zhou, he forged an imperial command and told the Southern Tang ruler, "I have heard that Jiangnan's years of defiance were all Chancellor Yan Xu's doing. You should cut off his head on my behalf."

sentences.zh: 唐主知覺素與續有隙，固未之信。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler knew that Jue had long borne a grudge against Xu and therefore did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler knew Chen Jue had long hated Yan Xu and therefore refused to believe him.

sentences.zh: 鐘謨主覆之於周。

translations.literal: Zhong Mo argued the contrary at Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Mo argued the opposite case before Emperor Shizong at the Later Zhou court.

sentences.zh: 唐主乃因謨覆命，上言：「久拒王師，皆臣愚迷，非續之罪。」

translations.literal: The Tang ruler then, through Mo's return of report, wrote upward, "Long resisting the royal army—all my own folly and confusion; it is not Xu's fault."
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler then sent back word through Zhong Mo, reporting upward, "Our long resistance to the imperial army was entirely my own blindness and error—not Yan Xu's crime."

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，大驚曰：「審如此，則續乃忠臣，朕為天下主，豈教人殺忠臣乎！」

translations.literal: The emperor, hearing this, was greatly astonished and said, "If it is truly so, then Xu is a loyal minister—I am sovereign of all under Heaven; would I instruct men to kill a loyal minister!"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong, hearing this, was deeply shaken and said, "If that is truly so, then Yan Xu is a loyal minister. I am sovereign of all under Heaven—would I command anyone to kill a loyal man!"

sentences.zh: 謨還，以白唐主。

translations.literal: Mo returned and told the Tang ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Mo returned and reported this to the Southern Tang ruler.

sentences.zh: 唐主欲誅齊丘等，復遣謨入稟於帝。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler wished to execute Qiqiu and the others and again sent Mo to report this to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler wished to put Song Qiqiu and his faction to death and again dispatched Zhong Mo to seek Emperor Shizong's approval.

sentences.zh: 帝以異國之臣，無所可否。

translations.literal: The emperor, regarding them as ministers of another state, neither approved nor denied.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong, treating them as the ministers of a foreign realm, neither approved nor refused.

sentences.zh: 己亥，唐主命知樞密院殷崇義草詔暴齊丘、覺、征古罪惡，聽齊丘歸九華山舊隱，官爵悉如故；

translations.literal: On jihai, the Tang ruler ordered Privy Council drafter Yin Chongyi to draft an edict exposing the crimes of Qiqiu, Jue, and Zhenggu; Qiqiu was permitted to return to his old hermitage on Mount Jiuhua, his ranks and titles all remaining as before;
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, the Southern Tang ruler ordered Privy Council drafter Yin Chongyi to draft an edict denouncing the crimes of Song Qiqiu, Chen Jue, and Li Zhenggu. Song Qiqiu was permitted to retire to his former hermitage on Mount Jiuhua, his rank and titles unchanged;

sentences.zh: 覺責授國子博士，宣州安置；

translations.literal: Jue was demoted to National University Erudite and stationed at Xuan Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jue was demoted to Erudite of the National University and posted to Xuanzhou;

sentences.zh: 征古削奪官爵，賜自盡；

translations.literal: Zhenggu was stripped of rank and titles and ordered to commit suicide;
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhenggu was stripped of all rank and title and commanded to take his own life;

sentences.zh: 黨與皆不問。

translations.literal: their partisans were not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: their associates went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 遣使告於周。

translations.literal: An envoy was sent to report this to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy was dispatched to inform Later Zhou.

sentences.zh: 丙午，蜀以峽路巡檢制置使高彥儔為招討使。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Shu appointed Gao Yanchou, Inspector-General of the Gorge Route, Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Later Shu appointed Gao Yanchou, Inspector-General of the Gorge Route, Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 平盧節度使、太師、中書令陳王安審琦僕夫安友進與其嬖妾通，妾恐事洩，與友進謀殺審琦，友進不可，妾曰：「不然，我當反告汝。」

translations.literal: Pinglu military governor, Grand Preceptor, and Central Secretariat Director Chen Wang An Shenqi's groom An Youjin had an affair with his favorite concubine; the concubine, fearing exposure, conspired with Youjin to kill Shenqi; Youjin refused, and the concubine said, "If not, I shall turn and accuse you."
translations.idiomatic: An Shenqi, Prince of Chen, Pinglu military governor, Grand Preceptor, and Central Secretariat director, had a groom named An Youjin who was sleeping with his favorite concubine. Fearing discovery, the concubine plotted with Youjin to kill Shenqi. Youjin refused, and she said, "If you will not, I shall accuse you instead."

sentences.zh: 友進懼而從之。

translations.literal: Youjin, in fear, complied.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Youjin agreed.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸丑，審琦醉熟寢，妾取審琦所枕劍授友進而殺之，仍盡殺侍婢在帳下者以滅口。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on guichou, Shenqi, drunk, slept deeply; the concubine took the sword Shenqi slept upon and handed it to Youjin, who killed him; she also killed all the serving maids in the tent to silence witnesses.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on guichou, Shenqi lay drunk in a deep sleep. The concubine took the sword he kept beneath his pillow, handed it to Youjin, and had him kill him. She then slaughtered every maid servant in the tent to silence all witnesses.

sentences.zh: 後數日，其子守忠始知之，執友進等冎之。

translations.literal: Several days later, his son Shouzhong finally learned of it, seized Youjin and the others, and executed them by dismemberment.
translations.idiomatic: Days later his son Shouzhong learned what had happened, seized Youjin and his accomplices, and had them dismembered.

sentences.zh: 初，有司將立正仗，宿設樂縣於殿庭，帝觀之，見鐘磬有設而不擊者，問樂工，皆不能對。

translations.literal: Previously, when the officials were about to set up the formal guard, they had overnight set out the suspended musical instruments in the palace courtyard; the emperor viewed them, saw bells and chimes set out but not struck, questioned the musicians, and none could answer.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as officials prepared to mount the formal guard ceremony, musicians had overnight arranged the suspended instruments in the palace courtyard. Emperor Shizong inspected them, noticed bells and chimes in place but unplayed, questioned the musicians, and not one could explain why.

sentences.zh: 乃命竇儼討論古今，考正雅樂。

translations.literal: He then ordered Dou Yan to investigate ancient and modern practice and examine and correct orthodox music.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Dou Yan to study music ancient and modern and restore the orthodox scale.

sentences.zh: 王樸素音律，帝以樂事詢之，樸上疏，以為：「禮以檢形，樂以治心；

translations.literal: Wang Pu was skilled in pitch and tone; the emperor inquired of him regarding music, and Pu submitted a memorial stating, "Rites restrain the form; music governs the heart;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pu had long mastered pitch and tone. When Emperor Shizong consulted him on music, Pu submitted a memorial arguing, "Rites discipline the outward form; music orders the inner heart;

sentences.zh: 形順於外，心和於內，然而天下不治者未之有也。

translations.literal: when the form is compliant without and the heart harmonious within, there has never yet been one whose realm was not well governed.
translations.idiomatic: when outward conduct is orderly and inward disposition is at peace, no realm has ever failed to find good order.

sentences.zh: 是以禮樂修於上，而萬國化於下，聖人之教不肅而成，其政不嚴而治，用此道也。

translations.literal: Thus when rites and music are cultivated above, the ten thousand states are transformed below; the sage's teaching succeeds without severity, his governance without harshness—by this Way it is done.
translations.idiomatic: When rites and music are perfected above, the myriad states are transformed below. The sage's teaching takes hold without severity; his governance prevails without harshness—such is the Way.

sentences.zh: 夫樂生於人心而聲成於物，物聲既成，復能感人之心。

translations.literal: Music is born in the human heart, and sound is completed in things; once the sounds of things are completed, they can again move the human heart.
translations.idiomatic: Music arises from the human heart, and sound takes shape through instruments. Once those sounds are formed, they in turn stir the heart anew.

sentences.zh: 昔者黃帝吹九寸之管，得黃鐘正聲，半之為清聲，倍之為緩聲，三分損益之以生十二律。

translations.literal: In antiquity the Yellow Emperor blew a nine-inch pipe and obtained the Yellow Bell standard tone; halving it produced the clear tone, doubling it the slow tone; by subtracting and adding a third he generated the twelve pitches.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the Yellow Emperor blew a nine-inch pipe and drew forth the standard tone of the Yellow Bell. Halving it yielded the clear tone; doubling it yielded the slow tone. By the method of subtracting and adding a third, he derived the twelve pitches.

sentences.zh: 十二律旋相為宮以生七調，為一均。

translations.literal: The twelve pitches, rotating one after another as tonal centers, generate seven modes—this constitutes one key.
translations.idiomatic: The twelve pitches, each in turn serving as tonal center, give rise to seven modes—together forming one key.

sentences.zh: 凡十二均，八十四調而大備。

translations.literal: In all, twelve keys and eighty-four modes, and the system is complete.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve keys in all, eighty-four modes—the system stood complete.

sentences.zh: 遭秦滅學，歷代治樂者罕能用之。

translations.literal: When Qin extinguished learning, generations of those who restored music rarely could employ it.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin burned the books and broke the tradition of learning, generation after generation of music restorers could scarcely put the full system to use.

sentences.zh: 唐太宗之世，祖孝孫、張文收考正大樂，備八十四調。

translations.literal: In the age of Emperor Taizong of Tang, Zu Xiaosun and Zhang Wenshou examined and corrected the great music, completing eighty-four modes.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taizong of Tang, Zu Xiaosun and Zhang Wenshou restored the great music and brought the full complement of eighty-four modes to completion.

sentences.zh: 安、史之亂，器與工什亡八九；

translations.literal: In the An-Shi Rebellion, instruments and craftsmen were nine-tenths lost;
translations.idiomatic: The An Lushan–Shi Siming rebellion destroyed nine instruments and craftsmen in ten;

sentences.zh: 至於黃巢，蕩盡無遺。

translations.literal: By the time of Huang Chao, everything was swept away, nothing remaining.
translations.idiomatic: By Huang Chao's day the tradition had been swept clean—nothing remained.

sentences.zh: 時有太常博士殷盈孫，按《考工記》，鑄鎛鐘十二，編鐘二百四十。

translations.literal: At that time there was Grand Music Academician Yin Yingsun, who according to the Artificers' Record cast twelve bell-chimes and two hundred forty serial bells.
translations.idiomatic: In those days Grand Music Academician Yin Yingsun, following the Artificers' Record, cast twelve bell-chimes and two hundred forty serial bells.

sentences.zh: 處士蕭承訓校定石磬，今之在縣者是也。

translations.literal: Recluse Xiao Chengxun calibrated the stone chimes—the ones now in the prefecture are his.
translations.idiomatic: The recluse Xiao Chengxun calibrated the stone chimes; those now in the prefecture are his work.

sentences.zh: 雖有鐘磬之狀，殊無相應之和，其鎛鐘不問音律，但循環而擊，編鐘、編磬徒懸而已。

translations.literal: Though bells and chimes had the outward form, there was utterly no corresponding harmony; the bell-chimes paid no heed to pitch, but were struck in rotation; the serial bells and serial chimes were merely suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Bells and chimes kept their outward shape, but harmony was gone. The bell-chimes ignored pitch entirely and were merely struck in rotation; serial bells and stone chimes hung unused.

sentences.zh: 絲、竹、匏、土僅有七聲，名為黃鐘之宮，其存者九曲。

translations.literal: Silk, bamboo, gourd, and clay had only seven tones, called the Yellow Bell palace; of those surviving, nine melodies.
translations.idiomatic: String, bamboo, gourd, and clay instruments produced only seven tones in what was called the Yellow Bell key; nine melodies survived.

sentences.zh: 考之三曲協律，六曲參涉諸調。

translations.literal: Upon examination, three melodies accorded with the pitch; six melodies mixed into various modes.
translations.idiomatic: On review, three melodies held true to pitch; six drifted across the modes.

sentences.zh: 蓋樂之廢缺，無甚於今。

translations.literal: Truly, in the ruination and loss of music, nothing surpasses the present day.
translations.idiomatic: Never had music fallen so far into ruin as in our own day.

sentences.zh: 「陛下武功既著，垂意禮樂，以臣嘗學律呂，宣示古今樂錄，命臣討論。

translations.literal: "Your Majesty's martial achievements already accomplished, you turn your mind to rites and music; because your servant once studied pitch and tone, you displayed ancient and modern music records and ordered your servant to discuss them.
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty's martial glory stands established, and you now turn to rites and music. Knowing that I have studied pitch and tone, you laid before me the music records of antiquity and the present and charged me to investigate them.

sentences.zh: 臣謹如古法，以秬黍定尺，長九寸徑三分為黃鐘之管，與今黃鐘之聲相應，因而推之，得十二律。

translations.literal: Your servant has reverently followed the ancient method, taking black millet to fix the foot-length; nine inches long, three tenths in diameter makes the Yellow Bell pipe—corresponding with today's Yellow Bell tone—and from this deriving, obtained the twelve pitches.
translations.idiomatic: I have followed the ancient method: black millet grains fix the standard foot; a pipe nine inches long and three tenths across gives the Yellow Bell tone, matching the Yellow Bell pitch of today. From that I derived the twelve pitches.

sentences.zh: 以為眾管互吹，用聲不便，乃作律准，十有三弦，其長九尺，皆應黃鐘之聲，以次設柱，為十一律，及黃鐘清聲，旋用七律以為一均。

translations.literal: Considering that having many pipes blown in turn was inconvenient for use, I therefore made a pitch standard with thirteen strings, nine feet long, all responding to the Yellow Bell tone; setting posts in succession for eleven pitches and the Yellow Bell clear tone, using in rotation seven pitches to form one key.
translations.idiomatic: Because blowing many pipes in alternation is unwieldy, I devised a pitch standard of thirteen strings, each nine feet long, all tuned to the Yellow Bell. Posts set in sequence represent the eleven pitches plus the Yellow Bell clear tone; seven pitches in rotation form one key.

sentences.zh: 為均之主者，宮也，征、商、羽、角、變宮、變徵次焉。

translations.literal: What serves as master of the key is the gong; zhi, shang, yu, jue, bian gong, and bian zhi follow in order.
translations.idiomatic: The gong tone governs each key; zhi, shang, yu, jue, sharp gong, and sharp zhi follow in turn.
