sentences.zh: 發其均主之聲，歸於本音之律，迭應不亂，乃成其調，凡八十一調。

translations.literal: Emitting the tone that governs the key, returning to the pitch of its root tone, answering in alternation without disorder—then the mode is formed; eighty-one modes in all.
translations.idiomatic: From the key's governing tone, returning each tone to its root pitch, the modes answer one another without confusion—eighty-one modes in all.

sentences.zh: 此法久絕，出臣獨見，乞集百官校其得失。」

translations.literal: This method long extinct, emerging from your servant's unique insight—I beg to assemble the hundred officials to verify its gains and losses."
translations.idiomatic: This method has lain dead for ages; it springs from insight I alone possess. I beg that officials be assembled to test its merits and flaws.

sentences.zh: 詔從之，百官皆以為然，乃行之。

translations.literal: An edict approved it; all hundred officials deemed it correct, and it was implemented.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved it. All the officials agreed, and the new system was put into practice.

sentences.zh: 唐宋齊丘至九華山，唐主命鎖其第，穴牆給飲食。

translations.literal: Song Qiqiu of Tang reached Mount Jiuhua; the Tang ruler ordered his residence locked, a hole bored in the wall to supply food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qiqiu of Southern Tang reached Mount Jiuhua. The Southern Tang ruler had his house sealed and provisions passed through a hole cut in the wall.

sentences.zh: 齊丘歎曰：「吾昔獻謀幽讓皇帝族於泰州，宜其及此！」

translations.literal: Qiqiu sighed and said, "Long ago I offered counsel to have the abdicated emperor quietly exiled to Taizhou—small wonder this has befallen me!
translations.idiomatic: Qiqiu sighed and said, "I once urged that the abdicated emperor be quietly exiled to Taizhou—is it any wonder I have come to this!

sentences.zh: 乃縊而死。

translations.literal: He hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: He hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 謚曰丑繆。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Chou Miu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Chou Miu—Ugly and Erroneous.

sentences.zh: 初，翰林學士常夢錫知宣政院，參預機政，深疾齊丘之黨，數言於唐主曰：「不去此屬，國必危亡。」

translations.literal: Initially, Hanlin academician Chang Mengxi supervised the Xuanzheng Court, participated in secret policy, deeply hated Qiqiu's faction, repeatedly said to the Tang ruler, "If this sort is not removed, the state will surely perish in danger.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Hanlin academician Chang Mengxi had directed the Xuanzheng Court and taken part in confidential policy. He loathed Qiqiu's faction and repeatedly told the Southern Tang ruler, "Unless these men are removed, the realm will perish."

sentences.zh: 與馮延己、魏岑之徒日有爭論。

translations.literal: He had daily disputes with Feng Yanji, Wei Cen, and their ilk.
translations.idiomatic: He quarreled daily with Feng Yanji, Wei Cen, and their cohort.

sentences.zh: 久之，罷宣政院，夢錫鬱鬱不得志，不復預事，日縱酒成疾而卒。

translations.literal: After a long time, the Xuanzheng Court was abolished; Mengxi, depressed and without achieving his aims, no longer participated in affairs, daily drinking himself into illness until he died.
translations.idiomatic: In time the Xuanzheng Court was abolished. Mengxi, thwarted and bitter, withdrew from affairs, drank himself sick day by day, and died.

sentences.zh: 及齊丘死，唐主曰：「常夢錫平生欲殺齊丘，恨不使見之！」

translations.literal: When Qiqiu died, the Tang ruler said, "Chang Mengxi all his life wanted to kill Qiqiu—what a pity he was not made to see this!
translations.idiomatic: When Qiqiu died, the Southern Tang ruler said, "Chang Mengxi spent his life wishing to kill Qiqiu—what a pity he did not live to see it!

sentences.zh: 贈夢錫左僕射。

translations.literal: Mengxi was posthumously promoted to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxi was posthumously promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙子朔，命王樸如河陰按行河堤，立斗門於汴口。

translations.literal: Second month, bingzi new moon, ordered Wang Pu to go to Heyin to inspect river embankments, establishing sluice gates at the Bian mouth.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the bingzi new moon, Emperor Shizong sent Wang Pu to Heyin to inspect the river dikes and to set sluice gates at the Bian Estuary.

sentences.zh: 壬午，命侍衛都指揮使韓通、宣徽南院使吳廷祚，發徐、宿、宋、單等州丁夫數萬浚汴水。

translations.literal: Renwu, ordered Palace Guard commander-in-chief Han Tong and Xuanhui Southern Court commissioner Wu Tingzuo to mobilize tens of thousands of corvée laborers from Xu, Su, Song, Shan, and other prefectures to dredge the Bian River.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu he ordered Palace Guard commander Han Tong and Xuanhui Southern Court commissioner Wu Tingzuo to draft tens of thousands of corvée laborers from Xu, Su, Song, Shan, and other prefectures to dredge the Bian River.

sentences.zh: 甲申，命馬軍都指揮使韓令坤自大梁城東導汴水入於蔡水，以通陳、穎之漕，命步軍都指揮使袁彥浚五丈渠東過曹、濟、梁山泊，以通青、鄆之漕，發畿內及滑、亳丁夫數千以供其役。

translations.literal: Jiashen, ordered Cavalry Army commander Han Lingkun to lead the Bian River east from Daliang city into the Cai River to open transport for Chen and Ying; ordered Infantry Army commander Yuan Yan to dredge the Wuzhang Canal east through Cao, Ji, and Liangshan Marsh to open transport for Qing and Yun; mobilized thousands of corvée laborers from the capital region and Hua and Bo to supply the labor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen he ordered Cavalry Army commander Han Lingkun to channel the Bian River east from Daliang into the Cai River, opening transport to Chen and Ying; ordered Infantry Army commander Yuan Yan to dredge the Wuzhang Canal east through Cao, Ji, and Liangshan Marsh, opening transport to Qing and Yun; and drafted thousands of corvée laborers from the capital region, Hua, and Bo for the works.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，開封府奏田稅舊一十萬二千餘頃，今按行得羨田四萬二千餘頃，敕減三萬八千頃。

translations.literal: Dinghai, Kaifeng Prefecture reported old field tax was one hundred two thousand-odd qing; now upon inspection found surplus fields of forty-two thousand-odd qing; edict reduced thirty-eight thousand qing.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Kaifeng Prefecture reported that registered taxable fields had totaled a hundred and two thousand-odd qing; a fresh survey found forty-two thousand-odd qing of surplus fields on the rolls. An edict cut the surplus by thirty-eight thousand qing.

sentences.zh: 諸州行田使還，所奏羨田，減之仿此。

translations.literal: Field-survey envoys returned from the prefectures; surplus fields they reported were reduced on the same principle.
translations.idiomatic: When field-survey envoys returned from the prefectures, surplus lands they reported were trimmed by the same rule.

sentences.zh: 淮南饑，上命以米貸之。

translations.literal: Huainan suffered famine; the emperor ordered grain lent out.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan was stricken with famine. Emperor Shizong ordered grain distributed on loan.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「民貧，恐不能償。」

translations.literal: Someone said, "The people are poor—I fear they cannot repay.
translations.idiomatic: Some said, "The people are impoverished—they may not be able to repay."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「民吾子也，安有子倒懸而父不為之解哉！

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The people are my children—how could a father fail to aid his children when they hang upside down!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong said, "The people are my children. Would a father refuse to save a child hanging upside down?

sentences.zh: 安在責其必償也！」

translations.literal: Why insist on demanding repayment!"
translations.idiomatic: Why demand repayment at all!

sentences.zh: 庚申，樞密使王樸卒。

translations.literal: Gengshen, Privy Council commissioner Wang Pu died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Privy Council commissioner Wang Pu died.

sentences.zh: 上臨其喪，以玉鉞卓地，慟哭數四，不能自止。

translations.literal: The emperor attended his funeral, struck the jade axe on the ground, wailed several times, unable to stop himself.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong attended the funeral, struck the jade ceremonial axe on the ground, and wept again and again, unable to stop.

sentences.zh: 樸性剛而銳敏，智略過人，上以是惜之。

translations.literal: Pu's nature was firm, sharp and keen; his wisdom and stratagem surpassed others—the emperor for this reason valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was hard by nature yet keenly brilliant, his counsel surpassing other men's—Emperor Shizong treasured him for it.

sentences.zh: 甲子，詔以北鄙未復，將幸滄州，命義武節度使孫行友扞西山路，以宣徽南院使吳廷祚權東京留守、判開封府事，三司使張美權大內都部署。

translations.literal: Jiazi, edict because the northern frontier was not yet recovered, the emperor would proceed to Cangzhou; ordered Yiwu military governor Sun Xingyou to guard the western mountain route; Wu Tingzuo acting Eastern Capital regent and acting Kaifeng prefect; Three Departments commissioner Zhang Mei acting Grand Inner Palace deployment commander.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi an edict announced that, with the northern frontier still unrestored, Emperor Shizong would travel to Cangzhou. Sun Xingyou, Yiwu military governor, was to hold the western mountain route; Wu Tingzuo was named acting Eastern Capital regent and Kaifeng prefect; Zhang Mei, Three Departments commissioner, acting commander of the Grand Inner Palace deployment.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，命侍衛親軍都虞侯韓通等將水陸軍先發。

translations.literal: Dingmao, ordered Palace Guard deputy commander Han Tong and others to lead land and water armies to depart first.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao he ordered Palace Guard deputy commander Han Tong and others to lead the land and river forces forward.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，上發大梁。

translations.literal: Jiaxu, the emperor departed Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Emperor Shizong marched out from Daliang.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚寅，韓通奏自滄州治水道入契丹境，柵於乾寧軍南，補壞防，開游口三十六，遂通瀛、莫。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, gengyin, Han Tong reported that from Cangzhou he opened a water route into Khitan territory, fortified south of Qianning Army, repaired broken dikes, opened thirty-six drainage mouths, and thereby connected Ying and Mo.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on gengyin, Han Tong reported that from Cangzhou he had opened a waterway into Khitan territory, fortified south of Qianning Army, patched broken levees, cut thirty-six drainage channels, and thereby linked Ying and Mo.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，上至滄州，即日帥步騎數萬發滄州，直趨契丹之境。

translations.literal: Xinmao, the emperor reached Cangzhou; that same day led several tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry out of Cangzhou, heading straight for Khitan territory.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Emperor Shizong reached Cangzhou and the same day led tens of thousands of foot and horse out of the city, driving straight into Khitan lands.

sentences.zh: 河北州縣非車駕所過，民間皆不之知。

translations.literal: In Hebei prefectures and counties not passed by the imperial carriage, the common people all did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: In Hebei towns and counties the imperial train did not pass, the people knew nothing of the campaign.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，上至乾寧軍，契丹寧州刺史王洪舉城降。

translations.literal: Renchen, the emperor reached Qianning Army; Khitan Ningzhou prefect Wang Hong surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Emperor Shizong reached Qianning Army. Wang Hong, Khitan prefect of Ningzhou, surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 乙未，大治水軍，分命諸將水陸俱下，以韓通為陸路都部署，太祖皇帝為水路都部署。

translations.literal: Yiwei, greatly built up the water army, separately ordering the generals land and water to advance together; Han Tong as land-route supreme commander, Taizu emperor as water-route supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei he greatly strengthened the river fleet and ordered his generals to advance together by land and water—Han Tong as land-route supreme commander, and Taizu Emperor as water-route supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，上御龍舟沿流而北，舳艫相連數十里。

translations.literal: Dingyou, the emperor boarded the dragon boat and proceeded north along the stream; ships connected for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou Emperor Shizong boarded the imperial dragon barge and sailed north; the fleet stretched bow to stern for tens of li.

sentences.zh: 己亥，至獨流口，溯流而西。

translations.literal: Jihai, reached Duliukou, went upstream to the west.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai he reached Duliukou and turned upstream to the west.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，至益津關，契丹守將終廷暉以城降。

translations.literal: Xinchou, reached Yijin Pass; Khitan defending general Zhong Tinghui surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou he reached Yijin Pass. Zhong Tinghui, the Khitan garrison commander, surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 自是以西，水路漸隘，不能勝巨艦，乃捨之。

translations.literal: From this point westward, the water route gradually narrowed and could not accommodate great ships, so they were abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: From there westward the waterways grew ever shallower, too narrow for the great warships, and they were left behind.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，上登陸而西，宿於野次，侍衛之士不及一旅，從官皆恐懼。

translations.literal: On renyin, the emperor went ashore and marched west, lodging in a field encampment; the guards numbered less than five hundred, and the attending officials were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Emperor Shizong disembarked and marched west, bivouacking in the open country. His escort amounted to less than five hundred men, and every official in his train was terrified.

sentences.zh: 胡騎連群出其左右，不敢逼。

translations.literal: Khitan horsemen in groups came out on his left and right but did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: Bands of Khitan horsemen rode out on either flank, yet none dared close in.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，太祖皇帝先至瓦橋關，契丹守將姚內斌舉城降，上入瓦橋關。

translations.literal: On guimao, Taizu Emperor Zhao Kuangyin arrived first at Waqiao Pass; the Khitan garrison commander Yao Neibin surrendered the city with all its defenders, and the emperor entered Waqiao Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao the future Song Taizu, Zhao Kuangyin, reached Waqiao Pass ahead of the main force. Yao Neibin, the Khitan commander there, surrendered the city, and Emperor Shizong entered the pass.

sentences.zh: 內斌，平州人也。

translations.literal: Neibin was a man of Ping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Neibin was from Ping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，契丹莫州刺史劉楚信舉城降。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Liu Chuxin, military governor of Mo Prefecture under the Khitan, surrendered the city with all its defenders.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen Liu Chuxin, Khitan prefect of Mo, surrendered his city.

sentences.zh: 正月，乙巳朔，侍衛親軍都揮使、天平節度使李重進等始引兵繼至，契丹瀛州刺史高彥暉舉城降。

translations.literal: In the first month, on the yisi new moon, Li Chongjin, commander-in-chief of the Personal Guard and military governor of Tianping, at last led his troops to arrive; Gao Yanhui, military governor of Ying Prefecture under the Khitan, surrendered the city with all its defenders.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month, on the yisi new moon, Li Chongjin, commander-in-chief of the Personal Guard and military governor of Tianping, at last arrived with his troops. Gao Yanhui, Khitan prefect of Ying, surrendered his city as well.

sentences.zh: 彥暉，薊州人也。

translations.literal: Yanhui was a man of Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui was a native of Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 於是關南悉平。

translations.literal: Thereupon all of Guannan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the entire Guannan region was secured.

sentences.zh: 丙午，宴諸將於行宮，議取幽州。

translations.literal: On bingwu, he feasted the generals at the field palace and discussed taking You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu he held a banquet for his generals at the field palace and debated the capture of You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 諸將以為：「陛下離京四十二日，兵不血刃，取燕南之地，此不世之功也，今虜騎皆聚幽州之北，未宜深入。」

translations.literal: The generals held that: "Your Majesty has been away from the capital for forty-two days; without bloodshed you have taken the lands south of Yan—this is achievement without parallel. Now the enemy horsemen are all gathered north of You Prefecture; it is not yet advisable to push deep.
translations.idiomatic: The generals argued, "Your Majesty has been absent from the capital forty-two days. Without drawing a blade you have taken all the lands south of Yan—an achievement without parallel in any age. The enemy cavalry are massed north of You Prefecture now; a deeper thrust would be unwise.

sentences.zh: 上不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 是日，趣先鋒都指揮使劉重進先發，據固安。

translations.literal: That day, he urged Vanguard Commander-in-Chief Liu Chongjin to set out first and seize Gu'an.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he ordered Vanguard Commander Liu Chongjin to march out ahead and occupy Gu'an.

sentences.zh: 上自至安陽水，命作橋，會日暮，還宿瓦橋，是日，上不豫而止。

translations.literal: The emperor personally went to the Anyang River, ordered a bridge built; as night fell he returned to lodge at Waqiao. That day, because the emperor was unwell, he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went in person to the Anyang River and ordered a bridge built, but dusk came and he returned to Waqiao to lodge. That day illness overtook him, and the advance halted.

sentences.zh: 契丹主遣使者日馳七百里詣晉陽，命北漢主發兵撓周邊，聞上南歸，乃罷兵。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler sent envoys who raced seven hundred li a day to Jinyang, ordering the Northern Han ruler to raise troops and harass Zhou's borders; when he heard the emperor was returning south, he then dismissed the troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan khan sent envoys galloping seven hundred li a day to Jinyang, ordering the Northern Han ruler to raid Zhou's frontiers. When word came that the emperor was heading south, the operation was called off.

sentences.zh: 戊申，孫行友奏拔易州，擒契丹刺史李在欽，獻之，斬於軍市。

translations.literal: On wushen, Sun Xingyou memorialized that he had taken Yi Prefecture, captured the Khitan prefect Li Zaiqin, presented him, and executed him in the army market.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Sun Xingyou reported the capture of Yi Prefecture and the taking of Khitan prefect Li Zaiqin, who was presented to the emperor and beheaded in the army market.

sentences.zh: 己酉，以瓦橋關為雄州，割容城、歸義二縣隸之。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Waqiao Pass was made Xiong Prefecture, and Rongcheng and Guiyi counties were cut off and placed under its jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Waqiao Pass was established as Xiong Prefecture, with Rongcheng and Guiyi counties placed under its administration.

sentences.zh: 以益津關為霸州，割文安、大城二縣隸之。

translations.literal: Yijin Pass was made Ba Prefecture, and Wen'an and Dacheng counties were cut off and placed under its jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Yijin Pass became Ba Prefecture, administering Wen'an and Dacheng counties.

sentences.zh: 發濱、棣丁夫數千城霸州，命韓通董其役。

translations.literal: Several thousand corvée laborers from Bin and Di were mobilized to wall Ba Prefecture, and Han Tong was ordered to oversee the work.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand conscript laborers from Bin and Di were mobilized to fortify Ba Prefecture under Han Tong's supervision.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，命李重進將兵出土門，擊北漢。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Li Chongjin was ordered to lead troops out through Tumen Pass to attack Northern Han.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu Li Chongjin was ordered to lead an army out through Tumen Pass against Northern Han.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，以侍衛馬步都指揮使韓令坤為霸州都部署，義成節度留後陳思讓為雄州都部署，各將部兵以戍之。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Palace Cavalry and Infantry Commander-in-Chief Han Lingkun was made military administrator of Ba Prefecture, and Yicheng military governor acting administrator Chen Sirang was made military administrator of Xiong Prefecture; each was to lead his division to garrison there.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Han Lingkun, commander-in-chief of palace cavalry and infantry, was appointed military administrator of Ba Prefecture, and Chen Sirang, acting administrator of Yicheng, was made military administrator of Xiong Prefecture; each was to garrison his post with his troops.

sentences.zh: 壬子，上自雄州南還。

translations.literal: On renzi, the emperor returned south from Xiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi the emperor marched south from Xiong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 己巳，李重進奏敗北漢兵於北井，斬首二千餘級。

translations.literal: On jisi, Li Chongjin memorialized that he had defeated Northern Han troops at Beijing, cutting off more than two thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi Li Chongjin reported a victory over Northern Han forces at Beijing, with more than two thousand enemy heads taken.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，帝至大梁。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, the emperor reached Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Emperor Shizong arrived at Daliang.

sentences.zh: 六月，乙亥朔，昭義節度使李筠奏擊北漢，拔遼州，獲其刺史張丕。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the first day of the month (yihai), Zhaoyi military governor Li Jun memorialized that he had attacked Northern Han, taken Liao Prefecture, and captured its prefect Zhang Pi.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the sixth month, yihai, Zhaoyi military governor Li Jun reported a strike against Northern Han: Liao Prefecture was taken and its prefect Zhang Pi captured.

sentences.zh: 丙子，鄭州奏河決原武，命宣徽南院使吳延祚發近縣二萬餘夫塞之。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Zheng Prefecture memorialized that the Yellow River had breached its banks at Yuanwu; the Southern Court of the Palace Secretariat Commissioner Wu Yanzuo was ordered to mobilize more than twenty thousand corvée laborers from nearby counties to block it.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Zheng Prefecture reported a breach of the Yellow River at Yuanwu. Wu Yanzuo, commissioner of the Southern Court of the Palace Secretariat, was ordered to mobilize more than twenty thousand laborers from neighboring counties to stem the flood.

sentences.zh: 唐清源節度使留從效遣使入貢，請置進奏院於京師，直隸中朝。

translations.literal: Tang Qingyuan military governor Liu Congxiao sent envoys bearing tribute, requesting to establish a memorial office in the capital and report directly to the central court.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congxiao, Southern Tang military governor of Qingyuan, sent tribute envoys asking to establish a memorial office in the capital and come directly under the central court's authority.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，詔報以「江南近服，方務綏懷，卿久奉金陵，未可改圖。

translations.literal: On wuyin, an edict replied, saying: "The Jiangnan region has recently submitted; we are now devoted to soothing and embracing it. You have long served Jinling and should not change your allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin an edict answered: "The south has only lately submitted, and our task is to cherish and reassure it. You have long served Jinling—you must not change your course.

sentences.zh: 若置邸上都，與彼抗衡，受而有之，罪在於朕。

translations.literal: If we establish your residence in the capital and thereby contend with them, then accept and possess you—the fault would lie with me.
translations.idiomatic: If I were to establish your office in the capital, pit you against them, and then take you under my wing, the fault would be mine alone.

sentences.zh: 卿遠修職貢，足表忠勤，勉事舊君，且宜如故。

translations.literal: Your distant maintenance of tribute and duty fully shows loyalty and diligence; exert yourself for your former ruler, and let all remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: Your distant tribute and diligent service already testify to your loyalty. Continue to serve your liege as before, and let things stand as they are.

sentences.zh: 如此，則於卿篤始終之義，於朕盡柔遠之宜，惟乃通方，諒達予意，」唐主遣其子紀公從善與鐘謨俱入負，上問謨曰：「江南亦治兵，修守備乎？」

translations.literal: In this way, for you the obligation of constancy from beginning to end, and for me the proper conduct of winning the distant—this alone is the way to accommodate all sides; surely you grasp my meaning." The Tang ruler sent his son Prince Ji Gong Congshan and Zhong Mo together to enter court for an audience; the emperor asked Zhong Mo, saying: "Does Jiangnan also drill troops and repair defenses?"
translations.idiomatic: Thus you would honor constancy to the end, and I would fulfill the duty of cherishing the distant—only such accommodation suits us both; I trust you understand my intent." The Southern Tang ruler later sent his son Prince Congshan and Zhong Mo to court for an audience. The emperor asked Zhong Mo, "Does Jiangnan still drill troops and strengthen its defenses?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「既臣事大國，不敢復爾。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Now that we serve the great state as subjects, we dare not do so again."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Mo replied, "Having submitted to the great state, we would never dare do such a thing again.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「不然，曏時則為仇敵，今日則為一家，吾與汝國大義已定，保無它虞。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Not so. Formerly we were enemies; today we are one family. The great principles between me and your state are settled—I assure you there is no other concern.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong said, "Not so. Yesterday we were foes; today we are kin. The covenant between our states is settled—you need have no other worry.

sentences.zh: 然人生難期，至於後世，則事不可知。

translations.literal: Yet human life is hard to foretell; as for later generations, affairs cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: Yet no man can see what lies ahead, and in generations yet to come, nothing is certain.

sentences.zh: 歸語汝主：可及吾時完城郭，繕甲兵，據守要害，為子孫計。」

translations.literal: Return and tell your lord: while I am still here, complete your walls and ramparts, repair armor and weapons, and hold the strategic points—for your descendants' sake."
translations.idiomatic: Go back and tell your lord: while I yet live, let him complete his walls, sharpen his arms, and hold every strategic point—for the sake of those who come after.

sentences.zh: 謨歸，以告唐主。

translations.literal: Zhong Mo returned and reported this to the Tang ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Mo returned and relayed all this to the Southern Tang ruler.

sentences.zh: 唐主乃城金陵，凡諸州城之不完者葺之，戍兵少者益之。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler then walled Jinling; wherever prefectural cities were incomplete he repaired them, and wherever garrison troops were few he increased them.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler then fortified Jinling, repaired every deficient prefectural wall, and reinforced every understrength garrison.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：或問臣：五代帝王，唐莊宗、周世宗皆稱英武，二主孰賢？

translations.literal: Your servant Guang observes: Someone asked your servant: Among the emperors of the Five Dynasties, Tang Zhuangzong and Zhou Shizong are both called heroic and martial—which of the two rulers is the worthier?
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang observes: Once I was asked, "Among the emperors of the Five Dynasties, Tang's Zhuangzong and Zhou's Shizong are both hailed as heroic and martial—which of the two was the greater ruler?"

sentences.zh: 臣應之曰：夫天子所以統治萬國，討其不服，撫其微弱，行其號令，壹其法度，敦明信義，以兼愛兆民者也。

translations.literal: Your servant answered, saying: The Son of Heaven exists to govern the myriad states, chastise those who will not submit, comfort the weak, enforce his commands, unify his laws, earnestly establish trust and righteousness, and thereby cherish all the people.
translations.idiomatic: I answered thus: The Son of Heaven exists to govern the myriad realms—to chastise the rebellious, shelter the weak, give force to his commands, unify the laws, and bind the people in trust and righteousness, loving all beneath Heaven as one.

sentences.zh: 莊宗既滅梁，海內震動，湖南馬氏遣子希范入貢，莊宗曰：「比聞馬氏之業，終為高郁所奪。

translations.literal: After Zhuangzong had destroyed Liang, the realm trembled. The Ma clan of Hunan sent the son Xifan to offer tribute. Zhuangzong said: "I have lately heard that the Ma family's enterprise will in the end be seized by Gao Yu.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong overthrew the Liang, the realm quaked. The Ma clan of Hunan sent Ma Xifan to pay tribute. Zhuangzong remarked, "I have heard lately that the Ma family's legacy will one day fall to Gao Yu.

sentences.zh: 今有兒如此，郁豈能得之哉？」

translations.literal: Now with a son such as this, how could Yu ever obtain it?"
translations.idiomatic: With a son like this, how could Gao Yu ever wrest it away?

sentences.zh: 郁，馬氏之良佐也。

translations.literal: Yu was a fine aide to the Ma clan.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yu had been a trusted counselor to the Mas.

sentences.zh: 希范兄希聲聞莊宗言，卒矯其父命而殺之，此乃市道商賈之所為，豈帝王之體哉！

translations.literal: Xifan's elder brother Xisheng, hearing Zhuangzong's words, at last forged his father's order and killed him. This is conduct fit for marketplace merchants—how could it be the bearing of an emperor!
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xifan's elder brother Xisheng, overhearing Zhuangzong's remark, forged his father's command and had Gao Yu killed. Such was the cunning of a market huckster—not the conduct of a true sovereign!

sentences.zh: 蓋莊宗善戰者也，故能以弱晉勝強梁，既得之，曾不數年，外內離叛，置身無所。

translations.literal: In general Zhuangzong was skilled in warfare; thus he could use weak Jin to overcome mighty Liang. Once he had obtained the throne, within scarcely a few years, rebellion arose within and without, and he had nowhere to set himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was a master of war—that was how a weaker Jin brought down mighty Liang. Yet once he held the throne, within a few short years rebellion rose within and without, and he found nowhere to stand.

sentences.zh: 誠由知用兵之術，不知為天下之道故也。

translations.literal: Truly it was because he knew the art of using troops but did not know the Way of governing all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He knew the art of arms but not the Way of holding the realm—that was the whole of it.

sentences.zh: 世宗以信令御群臣，以正義責諸國，王環以不降受賞，劉仁贍以堅守蒙褒，嚴續以盡忠獲存，蜀兵以反覆就誅，馮道以失節被棄，張美以私恩見疏。

translations.literal: Shizong used trust and commands to govern his ministers, and used righteousness to require of the various states: Wang Huan was rewarded for not surrendering; Liu Renshan was praised for steadfast defense; Yan Xu was preserved for utmost loyalty; Shu troops were executed for treachery; Feng Dao was cast off for lost integrity; Zhang Mei was distanced for private favor.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong governed his ministers through trust and command, and held the realm to the standard of righteousness. Wang Huan was rewarded for refusing to yield; Liu Renshan was honored for holding firm; Yan Xu was spared for unwavering loyalty; Shu soldiers were put to death for their double-dealing; Feng Dao was cast aside for his broken integrity; Zhang Mei was distanced for trafficking in private favor.

sentences.zh: 江南未服，則親犯矢石，期於必克，既服，則愛之如子，推誠盡言，為之遠慮。

translations.literal: While Jiangnan had not submitted, he personally braved arrows and stones, resolved on certain victory; once it submitted, he loved it as a son, gave his sincere counsel fully, and made far-sighted plans on its behalf.
translations.idiomatic: While Jiangnan still resisted, he took the field in person beneath flying arrows, bent on conquest; once it submitted, he cherished it as a father cherishes a son, spoke with unreserved sincerity, and counseled for its distant future.

sentences.zh: 其宏規大度，豈得與莊宗同日語哉！

translations.literal: Such magnanimity and largeness of spirit—how could it be spoken of in the same breath as Zhuangzong!
translations.idiomatic: Such breadth of vision and largeness of heart—how can Zhuangzong even be named in the same breath!

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「無偏無黨，王道蕩蕩。」

translations.literal: The Book of Documents says: "Without partiality, without faction—the King's Way is vast."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: "Without partiality, without faction—the King's Way runs broad and clear.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「大邦畏其力，小邦懷其德。」

translations.literal: It also says: "Great states fear his strength; small states cherish his virtue."
translations.idiomatic: And again it says: "The great states stand in awe of his strength; the small states cherish his virtue.

sentences.zh: 世宗近之矣！

translations.literal: Shizong came close to this!
translations.idiomatic: Shizong came close to this!

sentences.zh: 辛巳，建雄節度使楊廷璋奏出北漢，降堡寨一十三。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Jianxiong military governor Yang Tingzhang memorialized that he had marched out against Northern Han and reduced thirteen fortified stockades.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Jianxiong military governor Yang Tingzhang reported that he had campaigned against Northern Han and captured thirteen fortified strongholds.

sentences.zh: 癸未，立皇后符氏，宣懿皇后之女弟也。

translations.literal: On guiwei, Empress Fu was installed; she was the younger sister of Empress Xuanyi.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, Empress Fu was enthroned; she was the younger sister of Empress Xuanyi.

sentences.zh: 立皇子宗訓為梁王，領左衛上將軍，宗讓為燕王，領左驍衛上將軍。

translations.literal: The prince Zongxun was enfeoffed as Prince of Liang and appointed General-in-chief of the Left Guard; Zongrang was enfeoffed as Prince of Yan and appointed General-in-chief of the Left Brave Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zongxun was made Prince of Liang and named General-in-chief of the Left Guard; Zongrang was made Prince of Yan and named General-in-chief of the Left Brave Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 上欲相樞密使魏仁浦，議者以仁浦不由科第，不可為相。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to make Palace Secretariat commissioner Wei Renpu chancellor; discussants held that because Renpu had not come up through the civil-service examinations, he could not serve as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to appoint Palace Secretariat commissioner Wei Renpu chancellor, but critics argued that because Renpu had not risen through the examination track, he was unfit for the post.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「自古用文武才略為輔佐，豈盡由科第邪！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "From antiquity assistants have been chosen for civil and military talent and strategy—must they all come through the examinations?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Since antiquity rulers have drawn on civil and military talent for their aides—must every one of them have passed the examinations?"

sentences.zh: 己丑，加王溥門下侍郎，與范質皆參知樞密院事。

translations.literal: On jichou, Wang Pu was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat; he and Fan Zhi were both made participants in Palace Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Wang Pu was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat, and he and Fan Zhi were both assigned to participate in Palace Secretariat business.

sentences.zh: 以仁浦為中書侍郎、同平章事，樞密使如故。

translations.literal: Renpu was made vice director of the Chancellery and Associate Grand Councilor, retaining his post as Palace Secretariat commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Renpu was appointed vice director of the Chancellery and Associate Grand Councilor while continuing as Palace Secretariat commissioner.

sentences.zh: 仁浦雖處權要而能謙謹，上性嚴急，近職有忤旨者，仁浦多引罪歸己以救之，所全活什七八。

translations.literal: Although Renpu stood at the center of power, he remained modest and cautious. The emperor's nature was stern and impatient; when close attendants offended his will, Renpu often took blame upon himself to save them, preserving seven or eight out of ten lives.
translations.idiomatic: Though Renpu held the levers of power, he stayed humble and careful. The emperor was stern and quick to anger; when those near him crossed his will, Renpu often accepted guilt in their place and spared seven or eight of every ten from death.

sentences.zh: 故雖起刀筆吏，致位宰相，時人不以為忝。

translations.literal: Thus although he had risen from a clerk's desk to the chancellorship, people of the time did not regard it as unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: So although he had climbed from a clerk's desk to the chancellorship, contemporaries did not think him undeserving.

sentences.zh: 又以宣徽南院使吳延祚為左驍衛上將軍，充樞密使。

translations.literal: Wu Yanzuo, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was also made General-in-chief of the Left Brave Cavalry and appointed Palace Secretariat commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yanzuo, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was also named General-in-chief of the Left Brave Cavalry and appointed Palace Secretariat commissioner.

sentences.zh: 加歸德節度使、侍衛親軍都虞候韓通、鎮寧節度使兼殿前都點檢張永德並同平章事，仍以通充侍衛親軍副都指揮使；

translations.literal: Guidé military governor and chief adjutant of the Personal Guard Han Tong, and Zhenning military governor and concurrent commander of the palace-gate duty roster Zhang Yongde were both promoted to Associate Grand Councilor; Tong also remained deputy commander-in-chief of the Personal Guard;
translations.idiomatic: Guidé military governor and chief adjutant of the Personal Guard Han Tong, together with Zhenning military governor and concurrent palace-gate commander Zhang Yongde, were both made Associate Grand Councilors; Tong continued as deputy commander-in-chief of the Personal Guard;

sentences.zh: 以太祖皇帝兼殿前都點檢。

translations.literal: the future Taizu Emperor was concurrently made commander of the palace-gate duty roster.
translations.idiomatic: the future Emperor Taizu was concurrently appointed commander of the palace-gate duty roster.

sentences.zh: 上嘗問大臣可為相者於兵部尚書張昭，昭薦李濤。

translations.literal: The emperor once asked Minister of War Zhang Zhao which ministers might serve as chancellor; Zhao recommended Li Tao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked Minister of War Zhang Zhao whom he might make chancellor; Zhao recommended Li Tao.

sentences.zh: 上愕然曰：「濤輕薄無大臣體，朕問相而卿首薦之，何也？」

translations.literal: The emperor, startled, said: "Tao is frivolous and lacks the bearing of a great minister. I ask about chancellors and you recommend him first—why?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, taken aback, said, "Tao is flighty and lacks a great minister's dignity. I ask who should be chancellor and you name him first—why?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下所責者細行也，臣所舉者大節也。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your Majesty reproaches small conduct; what your servant recommends is great principle.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Your Majesty faults petty behavior; what I commend is large-minded principle.

sentences.zh: 昔晉高祖之世，張彥澤虐殺不辜，濤累疏請誅之，以為不殺必為國患；

translations.literal: In the age of Jin Gaozu, Zhang Yanzhe slaughtered the innocent without cause; Tao repeatedly memorialized asking that he be executed, holding that if he were not killed he would surely become a national menace;
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin Gaozu, Zhang Yanzhe butchered innocents at will; Tao memorialized again and again demanding his execution, warning that unless he were killed he would endanger the state;

sentences.zh: 漢隱帝之世，濤亦上疏請解先帝兵權。

translations.literal: in the age of Later Han's Emperor Yin, Tao also memorialized asking that the late emperor's military authority be stripped away.
translations.idiomatic: under Later Han's Emperor Yin, Tao likewise memorialized to strip the late emperor of military authority.

sentences.zh: 夫國家安危未形而能見之，此真宰相器也，臣是以薦之。」

translations.literal: To see the state's safety or danger before it has taken shape—this is truly the caliber of a chancellor; that is why your servant recommends him.
translations.idiomatic: To foresee the realm's safety or peril before it shows itself—that is true chancellor timber; that is why I recommend him.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿言甚善且至公，然如濤者，終不可置之中書。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your words are very sound and utterly fair, but a man like Tao can never be placed in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your argument is excellent and perfectly fair, yet a man like Tao can never sit in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 濤喜詼諧，不修邊幅，與弟澣俱以文學著名，雖甚友愛，而多謔浪，無長幼體，上以是薄之。

translations.literal: Tao delighted in wit and banter and did not keep up appearances; he and his younger brother Huan were both famed for literary learning. Though deeply affectionate, they often traded coarse jests without manners between elder and younger; the emperor therefore looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Tao loved repartee and neglected decorum; he and his younger brother Huan were both celebrated for letters. Though devoted to each other, they bantered coarsely without regard for seniority, and the emperor therefore held him cheap.

sentences.zh: 上以翰林學士單父王著幕府舊僚，屢欲相之，以其嗜酒無檢而罷。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Hanlin academician Wang Zhu of Shanfu was an old subordinate from his princely mansion, repeatedly wished to make him chancellor, but set the idea aside because of his fondness for wine and lack of restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hanlin academician Wang Zhu of Shanfu had served him in his princely household, the emperor often thought to make him chancellor, but dropped the idea on account of his drinking and want of restraint.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，大漸，召范質等入受顧命。

translations.literal: On guisi, his illness became critical; he summoned Fan Zhi and others to receive his final testament.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi his condition turned grave; he called Fan Zhi and the others to receive his dying instructions.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「王著籓邸故人，朕若不起，當相之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Wang Zhu is an old companion from my princely residence; if I do not recover, you should make him chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Wang Zhu is an old friend from my princely days; if I do not rise again, you should make him chancellor."

sentences.zh: 質等出，相謂曰：「著終日游醉鄉，豈堪為相！

translations.literal: When Zhi and the others left, they said to one another: "Zhu spends his days roaming the land of intoxication—how could he bear to be chancellor!
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi and his colleagues withdrew, they told one another, "Zhu lives in the country of drunkenness—how could he serve as chancellor!

sentences.zh: 慎毋洩此言。」

translations.literal: Take care not to leak this remark.
translations.idiomatic: See that this is not breathed abroad.

sentences.zh: 是日，上殂。

translations.literal: That day the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor passed away.

sentences.zh: 上在籓，多務韜晦，及即位，破高平之寇，人始服其英武。

translations.literal: While still a prince he had largely cultivated concealment; after ascending the throne and defeating the rebels at Gaoping, people first acknowledged his martial brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: In his princely years he had mostly kept his light hidden; only after he took the throne and crushed the foe at Gaoping did people truly credit his martial prowess.

sentences.zh: 其御軍，號令嚴明，人莫敢犯，攻城對敵，矢石落其左右，人皆失色，而上略不動容。

translations.literal: In commanding troops his orders were strict and clear, and none dared violate them; when besieging cities or facing the enemy, if arrows and stones fell to his left and right all turned pale, yet the emperor scarcely changed expression.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded armies with orders so strict that none dared disobey; in siege or battle, though arrows and stones rained to either side and his men blanched, he barely stirred.

sentences.zh: 應機決策，出人意表。

translations.literal: He decided according to the moment and devised plans beyond what others expected.
translations.idiomatic: He seized the moment and laid plans no one else foresaw.

sentences.zh: 又勤於為治，百司簿籍，過目無所忘。

translations.literal: He was also diligent in governing; ledgers from every office—nothing passed before his eyes that he forgot.
translations.idiomatic: He was tireless in administration; records from every office crossed his gaze and nothing slipped his memory.

sentences.zh: 發奸擿伏，聰察如神。

translations.literal: In exposing fraud and ferreting out hidden wrong, his perception was uncanny.
translations.idiomatic: In unmasking fraud and digging out hidden crimes, his insight seemed almost supernatural.

sentences.zh: 閒暇則召儒者讀前史，商榷大義。

translations.literal: In leisure he would summon Confucian scholars to read earlier histories and discuss their larger meaning.
translations.idiomatic: In his spare hours he called Confucian scholars to read the old histories and debate their larger themes.

sentences.zh: 性不好絲竹珍玩之物，常言太祖養成王峻、王殷之惡，致君臣之分不終，故群臣有過則面質責之，服則赦之，有功則厚賞之。

translations.literal: By nature he did not love silk, music, or precious curios. He often said that Taizu had nurtured the wickedness of Wang Jun and Wang Yin, so that the proper separation between ruler and minister never held to the end; therefore when ministers erred he would rebuke them to their faces, and if they submitted he would pardon them; if they achieved merit he would reward them generously.
translations.idiomatic: He cared little for silk, music, or fine trinkets. He often remarked that Emperor Taizu had indulged the vices of Wang Jun and Wang Yin until ruler and minister could not keep their proper distance to the end; so when ministers slipped he confronted them openly, pardoned those who yielded, and richly rewarded those who served well.

sentences.zh: 文武參用，各盡其能，人無不畏其明而懷其惠，故能破敵廣地，所向無前。

translations.literal: Civil and military men were employed together, each bringing their capacity to full use; all fear his clarity and cherish his kindness, and thus he could break enemy forces, expand territory, and advance wherever he turned.
translations.idiomatic: He used civil and military men together and drew out each man's strength; all feared his clarity and treasured his grace, and so he shattered enemies, widened his borders, and marched wherever he aimed.

sentences.zh: 然用法太嚴，群臣職事小有不舉，往往置之極刑，雖素有才幹聲名，無所開宥，尋亦悔之，末年浸寬。

translations.literal: Yet his use of law was exceedingly harsh: when ministers fell short in the least matter of their duties they were often subjected to the extreme penalty; even those of long-standing talent and reputation received no leniency. He soon regretted this as well, and in his later years grew somewhat milder.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his justice was pitiless: the slightest failure in office often brought the death penalty, and even men of established talent and fame won no mercy. He came to regret this, and in his last years softened somewhat.

sentences.zh: 登遐之日，遠邇哀慕焉。

translations.literal: On the day he ascended to Heaven, far and near mourned and yearned for him.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, mourners near and far grieved for him.

sentences.zh: 甲午，宣遺詔，命梁王宗訓即皇帝位，生七年矣。

translations.literal: On jiawu the testament was proclaimed, ordering Prince of Liang Zongxun to succeed immediately as emperor; he was seven sui.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu the testament was read out, directing Prince of Liang Zongxun to ascend the throne at once; he was seven years old.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬戌，以侍衛親軍都指揮使李重進領淮南節度使，副都指揮使韓通領天平節度使，太祖皇帝領歸德節度使。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on renxu, Personal Guard commander-in-chief Li Chongjin was made military governor of Huainan; deputy commander Han Tong was made military governor of Tianping; the future Taizu Emperor was made military governor of Guide.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on renxu, Personal Guard commander-in-chief Li Chongjin took Huainan as military governor; deputy commander Han Tong took Tianping; the future Emperor Taizu took Guide.

sentences.zh: 以山南東道節度使、同平章事向拱為西京留守。

translations.literal: Shannan East Circuit military governor and Associate Grand Councilor Xiang Gong was made western capital defender.
translations.idiomatic: Shannan East Circuit military governor and Associate Grand Councilor Xiang Gong was appointed defender of the western capital.

sentences.zh: 庚申，加拱兼侍中。

translations.literal: On gengshen Gong was additionally made palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Xiang Gong was further named palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 拱，即向訓也，避恭帝名改焉。

translations.literal: Gong was formerly Xiang Xun; the name was changed to avoid the given name of the deposed Emperor Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Gong had been Xiang Xun; the name was altered to avoid the taboo of the deposed Emperor Gong.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，大赦。

translations.literal: On bingyin a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin a general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 唐主以金陵去周境才隔一水，洪州險固居上游，集群臣議徙都之。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler, because Jinling was only one watercourse from Zhou territory and Hongzhou was strategically strong and lay upstream, gathered his ministers to discuss moving the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Tang ruler, seeing Jinling separated from Zhou by only a strip of water while Hongzhou was defensible and lay upstream, convened his ministers to debate relocating the capital.

sentences.zh: 群臣多不欲徙，惟樞密副使、給事中唐鎬勸之，乃命經營豫章為都城之制。

translations.literal: Most ministers did not wish to move; only Palace Secretariat deputy commissioner and giving-office attendant Tang Gao urged it, and he was therefore ordered to lay out Yuzhang as the form of a capital city.
translations.idiomatic: Most ministers opposed the move; only Palace Secretariat deputy commissioner and giving-office attendant Tang Gao pressed for it, and he was ordered to plan Yuzhang on the model of a capital.

sentences.zh: 唐自淮上用兵及割江北，臣事於周，歲時貢獻，府藏空竭，錢益少，物價騰貴。

translations.literal: From Tang's use of force on the Huai and the cession of land north of the river, its submission to Zhou as a vassal, and its yearly tribute and gifts, the treasury was emptied bare; money grew ever scarcer and prices soared.
translations.idiomatic: Since Tang had fought on the Huai, ceded territory north of the river, and served Zhou with yearly tribute, its coffers were drained; cash grew scarce and prices climbed.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎鐘謨請鑄大錢，一當五十。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Zhong Mo petitioned to cast great coins worth fifty each.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Rites Zhong Mo asked to mint large coins valued at fifty to one.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人韓熙載請鑄鐵錢。

translations.literal: Secretariat drafting officer Han Xizai petitioned to cast iron coins.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat drafting officer Han Xizai proposed casting iron coinage.

sentences.zh: 唐主始皆不從，謨陳請不已，乃從之。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler at first accepted neither; Mo pressed his plea without cease, and he was finally obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang ruler at first refused both proposals; Mo pleaded without relenting until he won consent.

sentences.zh: 是月，始鑄當十大錢，文曰「永通泉貨」，又鑄當二錢，文曰「唐國通寶」，與開元錢並行。

translations.literal: That month they first cast great coins worth ten each, inscribed "Eternal Circulation currency"; they also cast coins worth two each, inscribed "Tang state universal treasure," to circulate alongside Kaiyuan coins.
translations.idiomatic: That month they first minted ten-for-one great coins bearing the inscription Eternal Circulation currency, and two-for-one coins inscribed Tang state universal treasure, to circulate together with Kaiyuan cash.

sentences.zh: 八月，戊子，蜀主以李昊領武信節度使，右補闕李起上言：「故事，宰相無領方鎮者。」

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on wuzi, the Shu ruler had Li Hao take charge of the Wuxin military governorship; Right Supplementation Censor Li Qi memorialized, saying, "By precedent, chancellors do not hold regional commands."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on wuzi, the Shu ruler appointed Li Hao to the Wuxin military governorship. Right Supplementation Censor Li Qi memorialized, "By precedent, chancellors do not hold frontier commands."

sentences.zh: 蜀主曰：「昊家多冗費，以厚祿優之耳。」

translations.literal: The Shu ruler said, "Hao's household has many superfluous expenses; this is simply to favor him with a generous salary."
translations.idiomatic: The Shu ruler said, "Hao's household runs to extravagance; this is merely a way to favor him with a generous stipend."

sentences.zh: 起，邛州人，性婞直，李昊嘗語之曰：「以子之才，苟能慎默，當為翰林學士。」

translations.literal: Qi was a native of Qiongzhou, upright and blunt by nature; Li Hao once told him, "With your talent, if you could only be cautious and silent, you would become a Hanlin Academician."
translations.idiomatic: Qi was a native of Qiongzhou, blunt and incorruptibly upright. Li Hao once told him, "With your gifts, if only you could hold your tongue and watch your step, you would rise to the Hanlin Academy."

sentences.zh: 起曰：「俟無舌，乃不言耳。」

translations.literal: Qi said, "Wait until I have no tongue—then I shall not speak."
translations.idiomatic: Qi said, "Only when I have no tongue will I fall silent."

sentences.zh: 庚寅，立皇弟宗讓為曹王，更名熙讓；

translations.literal: On gengyin, the emperor created his younger imperial brother Zongrang Prince of Cao, renaming him Xirang;
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, the emperor enfeoffed his younger brother Zongrang as Prince of Cao, renaming him Xirang;

sentences.zh: 熙謹為紀王，熙誨為蘄王。

translations.literal: Xijin as Prince of Ji, and Xihui as Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: he enfeoffed Xijin as Prince of Ji and Xihui as Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 九月，丙午，唐太子弘冀卒，有司引浙西之功，謚曰武宣。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on bingwu, Southern Tang Crown Prince Hongji died; the officials cited his Zhexi campaigns and gave the posthumous name Martial and Proclamatory.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on bingwu, Southern Tang Crown Prince Li Hongji died. The authorities cited his Zhexi campaigns and posthumously named him Martial and Proclamatory.

sentences.zh: 句容尉全椒張洎上言：「太子之德，主於孝敬，今謚以武功，非所以防微而慎德也。」

translations.literal: Jurong magistrate Zhang Bi of Quanjiao memorialized, saying, "A crown prince's virtue rests chiefly in filial piety and respect; to posthumously name him for martial achievement is not the way to guard against small faults and cultivate virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bi, magistrate of Jurong in Quanjiao, memorialized, "A crown prince's virtue lies above all in filial piety and reverence. To enshrine him under a martial name is no way to check small faults and guard one's moral conduct."

sentences.zh: 乃更謚曰文獻，擢洎為上元尉。

translations.literal: They therefore changed the posthumous name to Literary and Filial and promoted Bi to magistrate of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The posthumous name was therefore changed to Literary and Filial, and Zhang Bi was promoted to magistrate of Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 唐禮部侍郎、知尚書省事鐘謨數奉使入周，傳世宗命於唐主，世宗及唐主皆厚待之，恃此驕橫於其國，三省之事皆預焉。

translations.literal: Southern Tang Vice Minister of Rites Zhong Mo, who directed the Imperial Secretariat, had often been sent on missions to Zhou, conveying Emperor Shizong's orders to Li Jing; both Shizong and Li Jing treated him generously, and relying on this he grew arrogant and overbearing in his own state, intervening in the affairs of all three secretariats.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Tang Vice Minister of Rites Zhong Mo, who oversaw the Imperial Secretariat, had often gone as envoy to Zhou, bearing Emperor Shizong's commands to Li Jing. Shizong and Li Jing both treated him handsomely, and he grew arrogant at home on that account, meddling in the business of all three secretariats.

sentences.zh: 文獻太子總朝政，謨求兼東宮官不得，乃薦其所善閻式為司議郎，掌百司關啟。

translations.literal: The Literary and Filial Crown Prince oversaw court governance; Mo sought to hold an Eastern Palace office as well but was denied, so he recommended his favorite Yan Shi as Secretariat Drafter, controlling the opening and closing of memorials for all departments.
translations.idiomatic: The Literary and Filial Crown Prince had taken charge of court affairs. When Mo sought an Eastern Palace post as well and was refused, he put forward his protégé Yan Shi as Secretariat Drafter to control the routing of memorials for every office.

sentences.zh: 李德明之死也，唐鎬預其謀，謨聞鎬受賕，嘗面詰之，鎬甚懼。

translations.literal: When Li Deming died, Tang Gao had been involved in the plot; Mo learned that Gao had taken bribes and once confronted him to his face; Gao was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Gao had taken part in the plot surrounding Li Deming's death. When Mo learned that Gao had accepted bribes, he once confronted him to his face, and Gao was terrified.

sentences.zh: 謨與天威都虞候張巒善，數於弘第屏人語至夜分，鎬譖諸唐主曰：「謨與巒氣類不同，而過相親狎，謨屢使上國，巒北人，恐其有異謀。」

translations.literal: Mo was on good terms with Tianwei Army Vice Commander Zhang Luan; they often spoke in private at Mo's mansion until deep into the night. Tang Gao slandered them to Li Jing, saying, "Mo and Luan are not of the same temper and yet are excessively intimate; Mo has repeatedly served as envoy to the northern court, and Luan is a northerner—I fear they have some secret design."
translations.idiomatic: Mo was close to Tianwei Army Vice Commander Zhang Luan; they often dismissed attendants and talked alone at Mo's mansion far into the night. Tang Gao denounced them to Li Jing, saying, "Mo and Luan are not cut from the same cloth, yet they are uncommonly intimate. Mo has gone repeatedly to the northern court, and Luan is a northerner—I fear they are hatching some secret plot."

sentences.zh: 又言：「永通大錢民多盜鑄，犯法者眾。」

translations.literal: He also said, "The Eternal Circulation great coins are widely counterfeited by the people, and lawbreakers are many."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "The people are counterfeiting the Eternal Circulation great coins in great numbers, and offenders are everywhere."

sentences.zh: 及文獻太子卒，唐主欲方其母弟鄭王從嘉，謨嘗與紀公從善同奉使於周，相厚善，言於唐主曰：「從嘉德輕志懦，又酷信釋氏，非人主才。

translations.literal: When the Literary and Filial Crown Prince died, Li Jing wished to install his younger uterine brother, Prince of Zheng Li Congjia, as heir; Mo had once served jointly with Prince Ji Li Congshan on a mission to Zhou and they were close friends, so he told Li Jing, "Congjia's virtue is slight and his will is timid, and he is an ardent believer in Buddhism—not the stuff of a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: When the Literary and Filial Crown Prince died, Li Jing meant to install his younger uterine brother, Prince of Zheng Li Congjia, as heir. Mo had once served with Prince Ji Li Congshan on a mission to Zhou and they were on excellent terms, so he told Li Jing, "Congjia's character is light and his spirit timid, and he is a fervent devotee of Buddhism—not material for a ruler.

sentences.zh: 從善果敢凝重，宜為嗣。」

translations.literal: Congshan is bold, resolute, and steady; he should be the heir."
translations.idiomatic: Congshan is bold, resolute, and grave. He is the one who should succeed you."

sentences.zh: 唐主由是怒。

translations.literal: Li Jing was therefore enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 尋徙從嘉為吳王、尚書令、知政事，居東宮。

translations.literal: Soon Li Jing transferred Congjia to Prince of Wu, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, with charge of state affairs, residing in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Jing moved Congjia to Prince of Wu, made him Director of the Imperial Secretariat with charge of government affairs, and installed him in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，謨請令張巒以所部兵巡徼都城。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Mo requested that Zhang Luan patrol the capital with his troops.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Mo asked that Zhang Luan patrol the capital with the troops under his command.

sentences.zh: 唐主乃下詔暴謨侵官之罪，貶國子司業，流饒州，貶張巒為宣州副使，未幾，皆殺之。

translations.literal: Li Jing thereupon issued an edict exposing Mo's crime of overstepping his office; he was demoted to Vice Director of the Imperial University and exiled to Raozhou; Zhang Luan was demoted to vice commissioner of Xuanzhou; before long, both were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing then issued an edict denouncing Mo for usurping authority, demoted him to Vice Director of the Imperial University, and exiled him to Raozhou; Zhang Luan was demoted to vice commissioner of Xuanzhou. Before long both were put to death.

sentences.zh: 廢永通錢。

translations.literal: The Eternal Circulation coins were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Eternal Circulation coins were abolished.

sentences.zh: 十一月，壬寅朔，葬睿武孝文皇帝於慶陵，廟號世宗。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the first day renyin, the Sagaciously Martial and Filially Cultured Emperor was buried at Qingling; his temple name was Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the first day renyin, the Sagaciously Martial and Filially Cultured Emperor was buried at Qingling and given the temple name Shizong.

sentences.zh: 南漢主以中書舍人鐘允章，籓府舊僚，擢為尚書右丞、參政事，甚委任之。

translations.literal: The Southern Han ruler promoted Secretariat Drafter Zhong Yunzhang, an old colleague from his princely establishment, to Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Participation in State Affairs, and entrusted him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Han ruler promoted Zhong Yunzhang, once a colleague in his princely household and now a Secretariat Drafter, to Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat with a seat in government, and relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 允章請誅亂法者數人以正綱紀，南漢主不能從，宦官聞而惡之。

translations.literal: Yunzhang requested executing several lawbreakers to rectify discipline; the Southern Han ruler could not agree; the eunuchs heard of it and hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhang asked that several violators of the law be executed to restore discipline. The Southern Han ruler would not consent, and the eunuchs, hearing of it, came to hate him.

sentences.zh: 南漢主將祀圜丘，前三日，允章帥禮官登壇，四顧指揮設神位，內侍監許彥真望之曰：「此謀反也！」

translations.literal: Three days before the Southern Han ruler was to sacrifice at the Round Altar, Yunzhang led the ritual officials up the altar, looking about and directing the placement of the spirit tablets; Palace Internals Supervisor Xu Yanzhen saw this and cried, "This is treason!"
translations.idiomatic: Three days before the Southern Han ruler was to sacrifice at the Round Altar, Yunzhang led the ritual officers onto the altar, scanning the ground and directing the placement of the spirit tablets. Palace Internals Supervisor Xu Yanzhen saw him and shouted, "This is rebellion!"

sentences.zh: 即帶劍登壇，允章叱之。

translations.literal: He immediately mounted the altar with sword in hand; Yunzhang shouted at him.
translations.idiomatic: He drew his sword at once and climbed the altar. Yunzhang rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 彥真馳入宮，告允章欲於郊祀日作亂。

translations.literal: Yanzhen raced into the palace and reported that Yunzhang intended to revolt on the day of the suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhen galloped into the palace and reported that Yunzhang meant to raise rebellion on the day of the suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 南漢主曰：「朕待允章厚，豈有此邪！」

translations.literal: The Southern Han ruler said, "I have treated Yunzhang generously—how could this be!"
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Han ruler said, "I have treated Yunzhang with great favor. How could such a thing be!"

sentences.zh: 玉清宮使龔澄樞、內侍監李托等共證之，以彥真言為然，乃收允章，系含章樓下，命宦者與禮部尚書薛用丕雜治之。

translations.literal: Yuqing Palace Commissioner Gong Chengsu, Palace Internals Supervisor Li Tuo, and others corroborated the accusation; accepting Yanzhen's words as true, the ruler arrested Yunzhang, imprisoned him beneath Hanzhang Tower, and ordered eunuchs together with Minister of Rites Xue Yongpi to conduct a joint interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing Palace Commissioner Gong Chengsu, Palace Internals Supervisor Li Tuo, and others backed the accusation. Taking Yanzhen at his word, the ruler seized Yunzhang, bound him beneath Hanzhang Tower, and ordered eunuchs to join Minister of Rites Xue Yongpi in examining the case.

sentences.zh: 用丕素與允章善，告以必不免，允章執用丕手泣曰：「老夫今日猶機上肉耳，分為仇人所烹。

translations.literal: Yongpi had long been friendly with Yunzhang and told him he could not escape; Yunzhang seized Yongpi's hand and wept, saying, "This old man today is meat on the chopping block, about to be cooked by an enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Yongpi had long been Yunzhang's friend and told him there was no escape. Yunzhang took his hand and wept, saying, "Today this old man is meat on the block, soon to be stewed by his enemy.

sentences.zh: 但恨邕、昌幼，不知吾冤，及其長也，公為我語之。」

translations.literal: Only I grieve that Yong and Chang are still young and do not know of my injustice; when they grow up, please tell them for me."
translations.idiomatic: Only I grieve that Yong and Chang are still young and do not know how I have been wronged. When they are grown, tell them for me."

sentences.zh: 彥真聞之，罵曰：「反賊欲使其子報仇邪！」

translations.literal: Yanzhen heard this and cursed, "The rebel wants his sons to avenge him!"
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhen overheard and cursed, "The traitor means his sons to avenge him!"

sentences.zh: 復白南漢主曰：「允章與二子共登壇，潛有所禱。」

translations.literal: He again reported to the Southern Han ruler, "Yunzhang mounted the altar together with his two sons and secretly offered prayers for some purpose."
translations.idiomatic: He reported again to the Southern Han ruler, "Yunzhang went up the altar with his two sons and secretly prayed for something."

sentences.zh: 俱斬之。

translations.literal: All three were executed.
translations.idiomatic: All three were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 自是宦官益橫。

translations.literal: From this the eunuchs grew yet more overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: From that time the eunuchs grew yet more tyrannical.

sentences.zh: 李托，封州人也，辛亥，南漢主祀圜丘，大赦。

translations.literal: Li Tuo was a native of Fengzhou. On xinhai the Southern Han ruler sacrificed at the Round Altar and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tuo was a native of Fengzhou. On xinhai the Southern Han ruler sacrificed at the Round Altar and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以龔澄樞為左龍虎觀軍容使、內太師，軍國之事皆取決焉。

translations.literal: Before long Gong Chengsu was appointed Left Army Reverence Commissioner of the Dragon-Tiger Watch and Grand Preceptor within the Palace; all military and state affairs were decided through him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Gong Chengsu was made Left Army Reverence Commissioner of the Dragon-Tiger Watch and Grand Preceptor within the Palace, and military and state affairs alike were settled through him.

sentences.zh: 凡群臣有才能及進士狀頭或僧道可與談者，皆先下蠶室，然後得進，亦有自宮以求進者，亦有免死而宮者，由是宦者近二萬人。

translations.literal: Any minister with ability, any top-ranked jinshi, or any monk or Daoist worth conversing with—all had first to enter the silkworm chamber before they could advance; some castrated themselves seeking promotion, and some were castrated to escape death; thus eunuchs numbered nearly twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Any capable minister, any jinshi who had topped the examinations, or any monk or Daoist worth speaking with—all had first to pass through the castration house before they could rise. Some castrated themselves to advance; others were castrated to escape death. Eunuchs therefore numbered nearly twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 貴顯用事之人，大抵皆宦者也，謂士人為門外人，不得預事，卒以此亡國。

translations.literal: Those in power and influence were largely eunuchs; they called literati "outside the gate" and barred them from affairs of state—in the end the state perished for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: Those who held rank and power were almost all eunuchs. They called the literati "men outside the gate" and shut them out of affairs of state. In the end the realm was lost for this.

sentences.zh: 唐更命洪州曰南昌府，建南都，以武清節度使何敬洙為南都留守，以兵部尚書陳繼善為南昌尹。

translations.literal: Southern Tang renamed Hongzhou Nanchang Prefecture and established a southern capital; Wuqing military governor He Jingzhu was made garrison commander of the southern capital, and Minister of War Chen Jishan was made prefect of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Tang renamed Hongzhou as Nanchang Prefecture and raised a southern capital there. Wuqing military governor He Jingzhu was made garrison commander of the southern capital, and Minister of War Chen Jishan was appointed prefect of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 周人之攻秦、鳳也、蜀中忷懼。

translations.literal: When Zhou forces attacked Qin and Feng, Shu was seized with fear.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou armies attacked Qin and Feng, fear swept through Shu.

sentences.zh: 都官郎中徐及甫自負才略，仕不得志，陰結黨與，謀奉前蜀高祖之孫少府少監王令儀為主以作亂，會周兵退而止。

translations.literal: Director of the Office for Visiting Officials Xu Jifu, confident in his talent and strategy and frustrated in office, secretly gathered partisans and plotted to install Wang Lingyi—grandson of Former Shu's Founder, a Deputy Supervisor of the Palace Storehouse—as leader to raise rebellion; when Zhou troops withdrew the plot was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jifu, Director of the Office for Visiting Officials, proud of his talent and thwarted in his career, secretly gathered allies and plotted to set up Wang Lingyi, grandson of Former Shu's Founder and Deputy Supervisor of the Palace Storehouse, as their figurehead for rebellion. When Zhou forces withdrew, the scheme collapsed.

sentences.zh: 至是，其黨有告者，收捕之，及甫自殺。

translations.literal: At this time a member of the faction informed on them; arrests were made, and Jifu killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: At this time one of the faction turned informer. Arrests followed, and Jifu killed himself.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲午，賜令儀死。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jiawu, Wang Lingyi was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiawu, Wang Lingyi was condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 端明殿學士、兵部侍郎竇儀使於唐，天雨雪，唐主欲受詔於廡下。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician and Vice Minister of War Dou Yi was sent on mission to Southern Tang; snow was falling, and Li Jing wished to receive the edict beneath a corridor.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician and Vice Minister of War Dou Yi went as envoy to Southern Tang. Snow was falling, and Li Jing wished to receive the edict under a covered walk.

sentences.zh: 儀曰：「使者奉詔而來，不敢失舊禮。

translations.literal: Yi said, "The envoy comes bearing an imperial edict; I dare not depart from the old rites.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yi said, "I come bearing an imperial edict and dare not depart from the old rites.

sentences.zh: 若雪沾服，請俟它日。」

translations.literal: If snow should stain the robes, I beg to wait for another day."
translations.idiomatic: If the snow should soil our robes, let us wait for another day."

sentences.zh: 唐主乃拜詔於庭。

translations.literal: Li Jing then received the edict with obeisance in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing then received the edict with obeisance in the open court.

sentences.zh: 契丹主遣其舅使於唐，泰州團練使荊罕儒募刺客使殺之。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler sent his maternal uncle as envoy to Southern Tang; Taizhou regiment trainer Jing Hanru recruited assassins to have him killed.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler sent his maternal uncle as envoy to Southern Tang. Taizhou regiment trainer Jing Hanru hired assassins to kill him.

sentences.zh: 唐人夜宴契丹使者於清風驛，酒酣，起更衣。

translations.literal: That night the Tang people hosted a banquet for the Khitan envoy at Qingfeng Station; when the wine had gone deep, he rose to change clothes.
translations.idiomatic: That night the Tang hosts feasted the Khitan envoy at Qingfeng Station. When the wine was well advanced, he rose to change his clothes.

sentences.zh: 久不返，視之，失其首矣。

translations.literal: For a long time he did not return; when they looked, his head was gone.
translations.idiomatic: He was gone a long while; when they went to look, his head was missing.

sentences.zh: 自是契丹與唐絕。

translations.literal: From this, Khitan and Tang broke off relations.
translations.idiomatic: From that day forward, Khitan and Tang ties were severed.

sentences.zh: 罕儒，冀州人也。

translations.literal: Hanru was a man of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hanru was a native of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 臣光言：先奉敕編集歷代君臣事跡，又奉聖旨賜名《資治通鑒》，今已了畢者。

translations.literal: Your subject Guang states: First, by edict I was charged to compile the deeds of rulers and ministers through the ages; again, by imperial decree the work was granted the name Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance — and it is now finished.
translations.idiomatic: I, Guang, respectfully report: I was first commanded to compile the records of rulers and ministers across the ages, then honored with the imperial title Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance; that task is now complete.

sentences.zh: 伏念臣性識愚魯，學術荒疏，凡百事為，皆出人下。

translations.literal: Prostrate, I reflect that my nature and insight are dull and crude, my learning barren and thin; in every sort of endeavor I fall below others.
translations.idiomatic: I must confess that I am slow of wit and shallow in scholarship, outmatched in nearly everything I undertake.

sentences.zh: 獨於前史，粗嘗盡心，自幼至老，嗜之不厭。

translations.literal: Only toward the histories of old have I roughly devoted my full heart; from childhood to old age I have loved them without tiring.
translations.idiomatic: History alone has held my devotion from youth to age — imperfectly, but without weariness.

sentences.zh: 每患遷、固以來，文字繁多，自布衣之士，讀之不遍，況於人主，日有萬機，何暇周覽！

translations.literal: I have often grieved that since Qian and Gu the words have multiplied; even plain-clothed scholars cannot read them through — how much less a sovereign, with ten thousand affairs daily — what leisure to survey all!
translations.idiomatic: I have long lamented that since Sima Qian and Ban Gu our texts have swelled beyond any common scholar’s reach — let alone a ruler beset daily by the myriad cares of state.

sentences.zh: 臣常不自揆，欲刪削冗長，舉撮機要，專取關國家興衰，系生民休戚，善可為法，惡可為戒者，為編年一書。

translations.literal: I have often, not measuring myself, wished to cut away redundancy, gather the pivots, and take only what concerns the rise and fall of states and the weal and woe of the people — good to take as law, evil to take as warning — and make one annalistic book.
translations.idiomatic: I dared to imagine trimming the excess, distilling what turns on dynastic fortune and the people’s fate — examples to emulate and warnings to heed — into a single chronological history.

sentences.zh: 使先後有倫，精粗不雜，私家力薄，無由可成。

translations.literal: So that before and after have order and essentials and dross do not mix — but private means were slight, and no way to accomplish it.
translations.idiomatic: So the narrative might run in clear sequence, the vital separated from the trivial — yet on my own I lacked the means to finish.

sentences.zh: 伏遇英宗皇帝，資睿智之性，敷文明之治，思歷覽古事，用恢張大猷，愛詔下臣，俾之編集。

translations.literal: Prostrate, I encountered Emperor Yingzong, endowed with wise sagacity, spreading civil enlightenment, wishing to survey ancient affairs to expand the great design; graciously he issued an edict charging your subject to compile.
translations.idiomatic: Then came Emperor Yingzong — wise, cultivated, eager to survey antiquity and enlarge the realm’s purpose — who graciously commanded me to undertake the compilation.

sentences.zh: 臣夙昔所願，一朝獲伸，踴躍奉承，惟懼不稱。

translations.literal: What your subject long wished, in one morning was fulfilled; leaping I received the charge, fearing only that I might not be equal.
translations.idiomatic: A lifelong wish granted overnight: I accepted the task with alacrity, anxious only that I might fail it.

sentences.zh: 先帝仍命自選辟官屬，於崇文院置局，許借龍圖、天章閣、三館、秘閣書籍，賜以御府筆墨繒帛及御前錢以供果餌，以內臣為承受，眷遇之榮，近臣莫及。

translations.literal: The late emperor also ordered that I myself select and recruit official assistants, establish a bureau in the Chongwen Academy, permit borrowing books of the Longtu Pavilion, Tianzhang Pavilion, Three Institutes, and Secret Repository, grant imperial brushes, ink, silk, and privy funds for fruit and fare, with an inner attendant as receiver — grace such as close ministers seldom matched.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor further let me choose my own staff, set up an office in the Chongwen Academy, borrow from the imperial libraries, and supplied brushes, ink, silk, and stipends from the palace purse, with a eunuch liaison — favors few courtiers have known.

sentences.zh: 不幸書未進御，先帝違棄群臣。

translations.literal: Alas, before the book could be presented to the throne, the late emperor abandoned the multitude of ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Tragically, before the work could be presented, Emperor Yingzong departed and left us behind.

sentences.zh: 陛下紹膺大統，欽承先志，寵以冠序，錫之嘉名，每開經筵，常令進讀。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has succeeded to the great line, reverently received the prior will, honored it with a preface at the crown, bestowed the fine name; whenever the classics lecture opened, you often ordered it read in.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty inherited the throne, upheld our late sovereign’s intent, graced the work with your preface and its noble title, and at the classics lectures have often had it read aloud.

sentences.zh: 臣雖頑愚，荷兩朝知待如此其厚，隕身喪元，未足報塞，苟智力所及，豈敢有遺！

translations.literal: Though your subject is stubborn and dull, bearing such generous knowing treatment from two reigns, to dash body and lose life would not repay the debt; if strength and mind can reach, how dare I leave anything undone!
translations.idiomatic: Dull as I am, the kindness of two emperors leaves me owing a debt no sacrifice could repay; whatever wit I have, I dare withhold nothing.

sentences.zh: 會差知永興軍，以衰疾不任治劇，乞就冗官。

translations.literal: It happened that I was assigned to know Yongxing Commandery; because of decline and illness I could not bear heavy governance, and begged a nominal post.
translations.idiomatic: When I was posted to Yongxing, age and illness left me unfit for demanding office, and I petitioned for a lighter appointment.

sentences.zh: 陛下俯從所欲，曲賜容養，差判西京留司御史台及提舉嵩山崇福宮，前後六任，仍聽以書局自隨，給之祿秩，不責職業。

translations.literal: Your Majesty bowed to my wish, graciously granted indulgent care, assigned me to judge the Western Capital Remonstrance Bureau and to oversee the Songshan Chongfu Palace — six posts in all — still allowing the book bureau to accompany me, granting salary and rank, without demanding official duties.
translations.idiomatic: You indulged my request, gave me a gentle berth as Western Capital censor and keeper of Chongfu Palace — six nominal posts — yet let me keep my compilers, pay my stipend, and free me from other duties.

sentences.zh: 臣既無他事，得以研精極慮，窮竭所有，日力不足，繼之以夜。

translations.literal: Your subject, having no other affairs, was able to refine thought to the utmost, exhaust all I had; day’s strength insufficient, I continued into night.
translations.idiomatic: With nothing else required of me, I poured every faculty into the work, and when daylight failed, labored on by lamplight.

sentences.zh: 遍閱舊史，旁采小說，簡牘盈積，浩如煙海，抉擿幽隱，校計豪厘。

translations.literal: I surveyed old histories throughout, gathered minor tales beside, documents piled full, vast as smoke over sea; I plucked hidden truths, reconciled to the hair’s breadth.
translations.idiomatic: I combed the standard histories and sifted lesser accounts until the documents towered like a sea of mist, winnowing obscurities and weighing every discrepancy.

sentences.zh: 上起戰國，下終五代，凡一千三百六十二年，修成二百九十四卷。

translations.literal: Rising from the Warring States, ending at the Five Dynasties — in all one thousand three hundred sixty-two years — I completed two hundred ninety-four scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: From the Warring States through the Five Dynasties — 1,362 years in all — the history runs to 294 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 又略舉事目，年經國緯，以備檢尋，為目錄三十卷。

translations.literal: Again I briefly set forth item headings, years threading states, to prepare for inspection and search — a Catalogue of thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: I also drew up a concise topical index, year by year and state by state, for ready reference: the Catalogue in thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 又參考群書，評其同異，俾歸一塗，為《考異》三十卷。

translations.literal: Again I consulted the host of books, weighed their agreements and differences, and made them return to one path — Examinations of Discrepancies, thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: I further compared sources and harmonized their conflicts in Examinations of Discrepancies, thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 合三百五十四卷。

translations.literal: Together three hundred fifty-four scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: In all, 354 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 自治平開局，迨今始成，歲月淹久，其間抵牾，不敢自保，罪負之重，固無所逃。

translations.literal: From Zhiping, when the bureau opened, until now it is first complete; years and months prolonged — contradictions within, I dare not guarantee myself; the weight of guilt, truly nowhere to flee.
translations.idiomatic: From the bureau’s opening in the Zhiping era until this day the work has been long in the making; flaws surely remain for which I cannot answer — guilt I cannot escape.

sentences.zh: 臣光誠惶誠懼，頓首頓首。

translations.literal: Your subject Guang, truly fearful, truly trembling — kowtow, kowtow.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject Guang, trembling with awe, kowtows again and again.

sentences.zh: 重念臣違離闕庭，十有五年，雖身處於外，區區之心，朝夕寤寐，何嘗不在陛下之左右！

translations.literal: Again reflecting: I have been apart from the court fifteen years; though the body dwells outside, my humble heart morning and evening, waking and dreaming — when was it not at Your Majesty’s side!
translations.idiomatic: Though fifteen years have passed since I left court, my heart, humble as it is, has never ceased to attend upon Your Majesty, waking or asleep.

sentences.zh: 顧以駑蹇，無施而可，是以專事鉛槧，用酬大恩，庶竭涓塵，少裨海岳。

translations.literal: But seeing my lame stumbling, nothing to apply, therefore I devoted myself to brush and knife, to repay the great grace, hoping to exhaust a drop of dust and slightly aid the sea and mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Finding myself useless for anything else, I gave myself wholly to the pen, to repay your kindness — hoping a mote of effort might marginally serve the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣今賅骨懼瘁，目視昏近，齒牙無幾，神識衰耗，目前所為，旋踵遺忘。

translations.literal: Your subject now bears worn bones, fearing exhaustion; vision dims and nears blindness, few teeth remain, spirit and knowing decay; what I do at present, on turning the heel I forget.
translations.idiomatic: I am worn to the bone, my sight failing, my teeth nearly gone, my mind fading — what I do one moment slips from me the next.

sentences.zh: 臣之精力，盡於此書。

translations.literal: Your subject’s strength and energy are exhausted in this book.
translations.idiomatic: All my strength has gone into this book.

sentences.zh: 伏望陛下寬其妄作之誅，察其願忠之意，以清閒之燕，時賜有覽，監前世之興衰，考當今之得失，嘉善矜惡，取得捨非，足以懋稽古之盛德，躋無前之至治。

translations.literal: Prostrate, I hope Your Majesty will widen the punishment for rash composition, discern the intent to be loyal, in pure leisure’s ease from time to time grant perusal — overseeing the rise and fall of former ages, examining the gains and losses of the present, praising good and pitying evil, taking what is right and rejecting what is wrong — sufficient to magnify the splendor of examining antiquity and ascend to unsurpassed utmost governance.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to forgive this bold offering, see the loyalty in my intent, and in moments of leisure peruse the work — tracing past dynasties’ fortunes, weighing the present’s right and wrong, honoring virtue and restraining vice — so that your reverence for antiquity may crown a governance without peer.

sentences.zh: 俾四海群生，鹹蒙其福，則臣雖委骨九泉，志願永畢矣！

translations.literal: So that the myriad beings within the four seas all receive that blessing — then though your subject’s bones lie in the nine springs, the aspiration would be forever complete!
translations.idiomatic: May all under heaven share in that blessing; then though I lie in the grave, my duty will be done.

sentences.zh: 謹奉表陳進以聞。

translations.literal: Respectfully submitting this memorial to state and report.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully submit this memorial for your notice.

sentences.zh: 臣光誠惶誠懼，頓首頓首，謹言。」」」」

translations.literal: Your subject Guang, truly fearful, truly trembling — kowtow, kowtow; respectfully stating.”
translations.idiomatic: Your subject Guang, trembling with awe, kowtows again and again — respectfully yours.”
